# OpenMoHAA native Metal port: plan

Goal (verbatim, see CLAUDE.md): "Create a FULL macOS Silicon Metal native port of openmohaa, with the ultimate goal of stripping OpenGL entirely from the code by the time we're done, and only have it run Metal from start to finish. Look at all possible ways to improve performance while we do it, increase efficiency, etc. Make it as lean and robust as possible."

Branches: `metal` = this work, in the repository pstngh/MoHAA-Reloaded since 2026-10-23 (§3.1 #41: one branch per port, `metal` and `vulkan`; it was `metal` until 2026-10-20, `main` from then until 2026-10-23 (§3.1 #24), in pstngh/openmohaa-metal; until 2026-10-20 `main` was a mirror of upstream, openmoh/openmohaa a2f34019 at the start). Upstream is the remote `upstream`, merged as `upstream/main`.

## Closing summary (session 44, 2026-10-20)

**All phases are done (0–8).** The port is complete as planned: 44 sessions, 2026-10-16 to 2026-10-20, every phase pushed to `origin/metal`. What `metal` is now:
- **Metal from start to finish.** `renderer_metal` is GL1's front end (BSP, shaders, TIKI, effects) with a Metal backend: hand-written MSL compiled offline into one embedded metallib, a pipeline cache (`MTLBinaryArchive`) with each map's pipelines compiled during its load, GPU-resident world and static-model geometry, GPU skinning, no GPU wait inside a frame (async readback). OpenGL is gone from the tree and the binary since Phase 4 (`port/glcheck.sh`); GL1 survives only as the `gl` reference flavor for comparisons.
- **No SDL** since Phase 6: the window, display modes, keyboard, text and mouse are AppKit and GCMouse (`code/macos`), checked against SDL's event streams byte for byte (`port/kbreplay.sh`) and in the user's feel test.
- **Lean:** arm64 and macOS only (Phase 7a: the other platforms, the GL renderers, the update checker and curl deleted), one sealed ad-hoc-signed `openmohaa.app` with openal-soft 1.25.2 built from source inside it (7b, 7c), plus `game.dylib`, `cgame.dylib` and `omohaaded`.
- **Faster than GL1** (§2): the bench's work per frame 0.89–0.95 → 0.2045 ms (4.5×), p99 ~2300 → 476 µs (4.8×). **Lower latency** (§2 "The Phase 5 latency check"): pump → present at 250 fps in a window 10.0 → 2.0 ms p50 since Phase 2, exclusive 1.9, the Space 1.8 (p95 2.0); input age on screen 3.55 ms p50 with `cl_cmdRate 100` at render 480, 4.6 at stock 250.
- **Online-compatible:** the protocol, the server-side game code and the data formats are upstream's; `cl_cmdRate` (default 100, §3.1 #22; `cl_movefps` since §3.1 #32) sends what a stock client at that command rate sends, every step exactly the interval since §3.1 #34. Tested online by the user (sessions 18, 25, 39).
- **Looks like GL1** except the recorded differences (§3.1 #20: the alpha-tested draw order's tie pixels, the 32-light fix, brush models lit by every dynamic light since session 56, the chat and game messages clear of the compass since session 68, the crosshair drawn as boxes since session 70, walls kept whole at the near plane since session 78, `r_depthClamp`); the fixed views' baseline is `base-s78` (`base-s70` until session 78's `r_depthClamp` moved the depth range, `base-s68` until session 70 drew the crosshair as boxes, `base-s35` until session 68 moved the game messages below the compass).

What is left is optional, parked or needs the user (§6): the black window over the other displays in exclusive fullscreen (built in session 75 behind `r_blackOutDisplays`; measured in session 79 with both monitors on: it brings exclusive to the blanked Space's figures, so paced presents were removed and the covers are the one mechanism; its default, the by-hand checks and the user's feel test are left); the frame-cap suggestion (a §4b item never started; Game Mode on/off measured in session 64; low-latency vsync dropped by the user in session 63, §3.1 #37; audio latency became part of Phase 9, the native sound engine, in session 57); small measured CPU items; release builds (CI, notarization) only with the user. The README's "OpenMoHAA for Apple Silicon" section is the user-facing summary.

Since then: session 45 (2026-10-20) made CMake find Xcode's Metal Toolchain by itself (the folder of `xcrun -f metallib`), so the README's build no longer needs `-DMETAL_TOOLCHAIN_BIN` (Phase 8 "Session 45 result", §3.2 "Added in session 45"). Session 46 (2026-10-20) prepared the first public release, ad-hoc signed (§5 "Release 1", §3.1 #23): the port's own bundle ID `io.github.pstngh.openmohaa-metal` and release version 1.0.0 (the game's own version stays upstream's 0.83.0), the vendored libraries' license texts, `port/release.sh` (the zip), CI (`.github/workflows/macos-metal.yml`: the README's build on a clean macOS 26 runner, green), the verified steps for a quarantined download (clear the quarantine with `xattr`; "Open Anyway" isn't enough), and the release notes draft (`docs/RELEASE_NOTES_1.0.0.md`). Upstream had nothing new to merge. **Released as v1.0.0 the same day, with the user's OK**, then moved at their request to a commit that also has the game folder as the home for configs and data, no qkey or PID file, the pipeline cache for players, no intro videos by default and their icon (§3.1 #25–#28). After v1.0.0 the same session set more of the port's own defaults (§3.1 #29) and made the game one app: `game.dylib` and `cgame.dylib` inside `openmohaa.app`, no dedicated server (§3.1 #30). Session 47 audited those commits and rewrote them (§6). Session 48 (2026-10-22) looked for the freezes the user saw above ~500 frames a second: the server ran every usercmd at every render rate and condition, so no freeze reproduced; what was measured and fixed was the picture's unevenness at high frame rates: JayRewd's open step as `cl_cmdDisplay 1`, rewritten, and the world drawn at the frame's moment inside the millisecond (§3.1 #33, §6). Session 49 (2026-10-22) put the usercmds on the Vulkan port's fixed grid of server time (every step exactly the interval at any frame rate, several usercmds in a slow frame) and removed `cl_cmdDisplay`: the open step is the only display (§3.1 #34, §6). Session 51 (2026-10-22) measured notuern's 250 Hz sub-grid for starting events as an experiment (a shot's usercmd at the next 4 ms point: 2.7 ms sooner to the server, stuck walks only where its short steps meet a lip) and kept nothing: the user's call (§2, §6). Session 53 (2026-10-22) made it a real setting for shots and jumps, the grid going on after the early usercmd: `cl_movesubgrid`, on by default (the user's OK, after notuern's "Safe bet is shots and jumps only"; §3.1 #35, §6), before 1.1.0 is published. After session 56 the user chose a native sound engine with JayRewd's Omaha as the guide (§3.1 #36): **Phase 9**, whose survey and design session 57 (2026-10-22) did (our own mixer on Core Audio, the PC original's Miles behavior as the reference, slices 9b–9g; 1.1.0 doesn't wait for it). Session 58 (2026-10-22) did 9b, the mixer alone (`code/macos/macos_snd.c`, tested by `port/sndtest.sh`); session 59 9c, every sound effect on the native driver behind `s_native` (0 = OpenAL until 9e); session 60 9d, its streams, music, dialogue, movies and saves (Phase 9); session 61 9e, the user's listening checkpoint: every default kept, and `s_native` defaults to 1; session 62 (2026-10-23) 9f, headphone 3D (Apple's HRTF) as `s_speaker_type 1`, off by default (the user's call); session 63 (2026-10-23) 9g, openal-soft out of the tree and the app (`sndref` keeps the last OpenAL commit), with the user's `s_ambientvolume 0` (no song at all) and `cg_tauntsounds` (other players' taunts off at 0); the user's online test "Sounds fine": **Phase 9 is done**, and the app is Metal, AppKit and Core Audio with no OpenGL, SDL or OpenAL. After it the user sorted the open items (§3.1 #38): session 64 (2026-10-23) measured the five performance items and kept two, both exact: obj_team3's terrain −30 µs a frame (the split walk over the tris that can act, the geomorph's new vertexes alone; 103 → 73 µs) and the console's box pipelines compiled at startup instead of at their first draw; the CPU-skinned multi-pass shaders (≤ 10 µs a frame) and a wake-up for late presents (they don't pay one) not taken; macOS Game Mode measured: the same latency and mean frame work, the bench's slow frames slower with it on, the declaration the user's call (§2 "Session 64", §6). Session 65 (2026-10-23) did session 33's gameplay leftovers in the decoupled mode against a local server, getting on a ladder from the top and terrain walks on obj_team3: the server's side is stock's at the command rate (the grid's exact steps bounce more steadily against a slope too steep to walk, the player stuck there either way), and one display bug was fixed, a stray footstep in the first frames after prediction comes back (a ladder's foot, a mounted gun) (§2 "Session 65", §6). Session 66 (2026-10-23) released current `main` as v1.0.0 instead of 1.1.0, at the user's request (§3.1 #39): Game Mode retested first, at the user's request (session 64's slower tail is the first seconds after a launch; in play the same, so kept), then the first v1.0.0 deleted and v1.0.0 published again on 08f19e40 with CI's checked zip (§5 "Release 1"). Then, the same day at the user's requests: the icon's star fills the canvas, the README is the port's own, the repository is MoHAA Reloaded (pstngh/MoHAA-Reloaded) with this port on the branch `metal`, `com_maxfps` defaults to 125, and v1.0.0 moved to bdce5ca9 (§3.1 #28, #40–#42). Session 67 (2026-10-23) reviewed the user's other repository, pstngh/openmohaa-client, read-only, and ranked its commits as candidates A–J; session 68 (2026-10-23) brought the approved A–F into `metal`, each improved (§3.1 #43, §2 "Session 68"): `m_filter` 0 by default, the dead leftovers out (~23,000 lines), `cl_ctrlbindings` a cvar of its own, the player's config kept after a game-folder change, the HUD's per-frame work exact and ~4–7 µs a frame less (the bench −4.4%), the chat and game messages clear of the compass. Session 69 (2026-10-23) reviewed pstngh/openmohaa-vulkan's PR #3 (JayRewd's cut of the backend's surface-list CPU) read-only: its ~69 µs were mostly its own per-surface timers, which the PR doesn't contain, and the rest addresses costs `metal` already removed; at most two small exact items, ~0.5 µs a frame together, not queued (§6 "Where things stand (end of session 69)"). Session 70 (2026-10-23) put session 68's items into v1.0.0 instead of a new version, at the user's request (§3.1 #44): the release notes updated (the settings that work differently for an old config, `m_filter` and `cl_ctrlbindings`; a section for an earlier 1.0.0 zip; the config fix, the HUD, the chat), the tag moved to fb6008ea and the zip replaced by CI's checked zip of it (§5 "Release 1", "Session 70"). Then, the same day at the user's requests: the old sessions' files (~20 GB, to the Trash) and chats cleaned up, the user's game folder on the release with their config tuned, 14 GL-era cvars no longer registered, the crosshair drawn as boxes in one draw (openmohaa-client's idea, by default the stock image's shape, §3.1 #45), and v1.0.0 moved again, to f1541d96 (§3.1 #46); session 71's removal of headphone 3D was dropped from the history at the user's request, so 9f stays. Session 72 (2026-10-23) found why headphone 3D sounded "very tinny": Apple's HRTF has a resonance of +6 to +10 dB at 11–14 kHz for sounds in front, and session 62's −1.3 dB on its output, matched with white noise (whose power is mostly in that resonance), took the body down with it (the game's gunfire ahead −2.6 dB below 2 kHz and +5.9 at 12.5–16 kHz against stereo). A fixed EQ to the stereo pans' mean timbre over the horizon replaced the −1.3 dB, the user's choice after an A/B, and at their request it was folded into 9f's commit, `metal`'s history rewritten from there and force-pushed, v1.0.0 kept on f1541d96 (§3.1 #47, §2 "Session 72", §6). Session 75 (2026-10-29), after the user found exclusive fullscreen "less smooth than it was with original openmohaa on gl1", built two fixes behind archived cvars at 0, code only (the monitors were off): `r_blackOutDisplays`, still black covers over the other displays while the game is in fullscreen in front (the parked item), and `r_metalPacedPresent`, a display link that presents the newest frame once per refresh; their measuring is next (§3.1 #49, §3.2 "Added in session 75", §6). Session 76 (2026-10-29) brought pstngh/openmohaa-server's fix of the strafe and backpedal speeds (9407d96d) to `metal` and `vulkan`, at the user's request: the client's prediction and a server it hosts move as the original games do (§3.1 #50, §6). Session 77 (2026-10-29) reviewed JayRewd's eight `vulkan` commits of 2026-10-26/28 read-only, and session 78 (the same day) built three of them at the user's request: leaning in the Allied Assault campaign always on, `r_depthClamp` on by default (walls the view leans into stay whole; a recorded difference, the baseline `base-s78`), `cl_nullbinds` off by default (§3.1 #52, §6). Session 79 (2026-10-29) ranked what else could make exclusive fullscreen smooth, and that evening, with both monitors on, measured session 75's covers: `r_blackOutDisplays 1` brings exclusive at 480 to the figures of the Space while macOS blanked the other display (frames replaced 21–23% → 2–3%), so paced presents were removed and the covers are the one mechanism (§2 "Session 79", §3.1 #54, §6).

## 1. Findings (session 1 survey)

Paths are relative to `code/` unless they start with `cmake/`.

### 1.1 Build and targets
- CMake ≥ 3.25, Ninja. Options in `CMakeLists.txt:14-40`: `BUILD_RENDERER_GL1` ON, `BUILD_RENDERER_GL2` OFF, `USE_RENDERER_DLOPEN` ON, `USE_OPENAL(_DLOPEN)` ON, `BUILD_SERVER` ON, `BUILD_MACOS_APP` ON (`cmake/platforms/macos.cmake:7`).
- Targets: client `openmohaa` (.app bundle), server `omohaaded`, `renderer_opengl1.dylib` (moved into `openmohaa.app/Contents/MacOS` by `finish_macos_app`), `cgame.dylib`, `game.dylib`, plus launchers (broken on macOS: they read `/proc/self/exe`).
- Install layout: everything goes to `<prefix>/lib/openmohaa/`. `fs_basepath` defaults to the folder that holds the .app. Libraries are found in `Contents/MacOS`, then in `fs_basepath` (`sys/sys_main.c:511`).
- `cmake/platforms/macos.cmake:17-18` set **deployment target 11.0 and universal arm64;x86_64** as plain variables, which override `-D` flags. Phase 1 changed them to **26.0 and arm64** (session 2). Every renderer gets `-framework OpenGL` (`:15`); `cmake/renderer_metal.cmake` removes it again for the Metal renderer.
- `find_package(OpenAL)` picks Apple's OpenAL.framework, which has no `alext.h`, and the build fails. `port/build.sh` passes `-DCMAKE_DISABLE_FIND_PACKAGE_OpenAL=ON` (internal openal-soft headers; the library is dlopen'ed as `libopenal.1.dylib`, `client/snd_openal_new.cpp:124`). Nothing builds openal-soft locally, so `port/run.sh` links Homebrew's next to the exe.
- `cmake/libraries/jpeg.cmake:1` and `freetype.cmake:5` only worked when a GL renderer is built (widened for `BUILD_RENDERER_METAL` in session 2). There is also a `JPEG_DEFINTIONS` typo at `jpeg.cmake:22`; left as is, because fixing it adds `USE_INTERNAL_JPEG`/`JPEG_INTERNALS` to GL1's compile.
- Flex/Bison output is written into the source tree (`code/parser/generated`, gitignored). CTest finds no tests.
- Internal SDL is a prebuilt universal `thirdparty/libs/macos/libSDL2-2.0.0.dylib` (2.32.8). zlib, jpeg-9f, ogg, vorbis, opus, libmad are compiled from `thirdparty/`.

### 1.2 Renderer interface
- The real header is `renderercommon/tr_public.h`. `renderergl1/tr_public.h` is dead (`#if 0`). `REF_API_VERSION` is 14.
- `refexport_t` has 85 entries. Groups: frame/scene, 2D (`DrawStretchPic`, `DrawTilePic`, `DrawStretchRaw`, `Set2DWindow`, `Scissor`, `DrawBox`, `DrawLineLoop`, …), TIKI/model (`RegisterModel`, `LerpTag`, `ForceUpdatePose`, `TIKI_Orientation`, swipes, …), fonts (`LoadFont` .RitualFont, `DrawString`), images/shaders, MOHAA world queries (`LightForPoint`, `GetLightingForDecal`, `MarkFragments`, `inPVS`, …). `GetRefAPI` is at `renderergl1/tr_init.c:1847`.
- **Upstream bug:** `SwipePoint` and `DrawBackground` are never assigned and stay NULL, though cgame calls `re.SwipePoint` (`cgame/cg_swipe.cpp:221`). The renderer implements `RE_SwipePoint` (`tr_swipe.cpp:88`).
- `refimport_t` has 87 functions + 4 data pointers, including TIKI/skeletor imports (`TIKI_SetPoseInternal`, `GetFrameInternal`, `SKEL_GetMorphWeightFrame`, …).
- Loading: `CL_InitRef` (`client/cl_main.cpp:3190`). The `cl_renderer` cvar (default `opengl1`, ARCHIVE|LATCH) selects `renderer_<name>.dylib`, falling back to the default. Symbol `GetRefAPI`.
- `glconfig_t` (`renderercommon/tr_types.h:212`) is copied field by field into cgame (`client/cl_cgame.cpp:49-73`), so **its layout is ABI and must not change**. Fields actually read: `vidWidth/vidHeight` (HUD, UI, input), `isFullscreen`, `stereoEnabled`, `renderer_string`, `hardwareType`/`maxTextureSize` (cinematics).

### 1.3 renderergl1 (what gets ported; ~43k lines)
- **The renderer owns the window**: `sdl/sdl_glimp.c` and `sdl/sdl_gamma.c` are compiled into the renderer. `GLimp_SetMode` creates the SDL window + GL context, and `GLimp_Init` calls `ri.IN_Init(SDL_window)` (`sdl_glimp.c:1179`).
- qgl is loaded at runtime (`SDL_GL_GetProcAddress`, `sdl_glimp.c:262`) through X-macros in `renderercommon/qgl.h`. About 73 distinct GL entry points are used. qgl lines per file: tr_backend 142, tr_shade 124, tr_draw 66, tr_shadows 59, tr_sphere_shade 44 (debug lines), tr_init 39, tr_main 28, tr_image 28, tr_model 25, tr_surface 19, tr_sky 17, tr_cmds 14, tr_flares 11, tr_sun_flare 9, sdl_glimp 60. Terrain, BSP, world, font, util, static models and marks have none.
- Single-threaded command queue (no SMP). `GL_State` (`tr_backend.c:220`) maps `GLS_*` bits (blend, depth, alpha test incl. foliage thresholds, fog) to GL state. Other key functions: `GL_Bind`, `GL_SelectTexture`, `GL_TexEnv`.
- **2D is immediate, not queued.** `Draw_*`/`Set2DWindow` (`tr_draw.c`) call `R_IssuePendingRenderCommands()` and then draw at once (Set2DWindow calls `glViewport`/`glOrtho` directly). The UI calls Set2DWindow around the 3D view. A Metal backend must be able to encode at any point in the frame.
- `tr_shade.c`: client-side vertex arrays from `tess` (positions as padded vec4). Per stage, the CPU fills `tess.svars` (`ComputeTexCoords`/`ComputeColors`, deforms/tcMods in `tr_shade_calc.c`), then issues one draw. Two TMUs max (`DrawMultitextured` + `GL_TexEnv`). `MAX_SHADER_STAGES` 8, `SHADER_MAX_VERTEXES` 2048.
- **`R_DrawElements` (`tr_shade.c:163`): `r_primitives 0` picks glDrawElements only if `GL_EXT_compiled_vertex_array` exists. Apple's GL doesn't have it, so the default path is `R_DrawStripElements` with `glArrayElement` inside `glBegin`/`glEnd` (immediate mode). `r_primitives 2` forces glDrawElements, and the user plays with it.**
- `tr_shader.c`: MOHAA keywords (`nextBundle`, `animMapOnce/Phase`, `ifCvar`, `#if` blocks for `r_textureDetails`, `portalsky`, `spritegen`, `force32bit`, `clampTime`, `lightglow` deform; rgbGen `lightingSpherical`; alphaGen `tikiDistFade`, `heightFade`, `dotView`, `skyAlpha`; tcGen `environmentmodel`, `sunreflection`; tcMod `wavetrans`, `parallax`, `macro`; `nofog`).
- `tr_image.c`: its own TGA/JPG/BMP/PCX/DDS/GST loaders. `Upload32` resamples to power of two, applies picmip, generates mipmaps on the CPU (`R_MipMap`) and always uploads RGBA8. DDS uploads as S3TC (off by default). Gamma/overbright: `R_SetColorMappings` (`:2758`) enables overbright only with hardware gamma **and** fullscreen. Otherwise `R_LightScaleTexture` bakes gamma into the texels.
- Sky: Q3 skybox in immediate mode (`tr_sky.c`) and the MOHAA portal sky (`tr_sky_portal.cpp`, re-runs `R_RenderView`). Flares: Q3 flares read depth with `glReadPixels` (off by default); MOHAA sun/lens flares draw orthographic quads (`tr_sun_flare.cpp`).
- Fog: fixed-function **linear distance fog only** (farplane), with `GLS_FOG*` bits for view/black/white fog color. No Q3 fog volumes. Mirrors/portals: `glClipPlane`.
- Dlights: baked on the CPU into copies of the lightmaps and re-uploaded with `glTexSubImage2D` (`tr_light.c`, `R_UploadDlights`). Entities get dlights through sphere lighting (`tr_sphere_shade.cpp`, CPU per-vertex light-grid + light lighting).
- Also: `tr_terrain.c` (ROAM-style LOD terrain with CPU split/merge and geomorph), `tr_staticmodels.cpp` (static TIKIs skinned once at load), `tr_ghost.cpp` (CPU-animated textures re-uploaded each frame), `tr_marks_permanent.c` (`.dcl` decals), `tr_shadows.c` (stencil shadow volumes, immediate mode), `tr_font.cpp` (RitualFont through tess), `tr_util.cpp` (immediate-mode emulation into tess). Screenshots read back with `glReadPixels(GL_RGB)` (`tr_init.c:498`). Cinematics go through `RE_StretchRaw` (`tr_backend.c:1008`), which calls `qglFinish` and uploads each frame.
- `renderergl2` is maintained upstream but off by default. It also skins on the CPU. Not used by this port.

### 1.4 GL outside the renderer
- None in client/cgame/fgame/uilib. They draw only through `re.*`/`cgi.*`/`uii.*`. The leaks are `renderercommon/qgl.h` (includes `SDL_opengl.h`), `tr_common.h` (`#include "qgl.h"`, `image_t.texnum` is a `GLuint`, GLimp declarations), `new/tr_types_new.h` (`OPENGL_DRIVER_NAME`), and `sdl_glimp.c`/`sdl_gamma.c`. `tools/` and the gamespy samples have GL but aren't built.
- `cl_avi.cpp` video capture is effectively disabled. `CL_RefCIN_UploadCinematic` is an empty stub, so in-world videoMaps are unsupported upstream.

### 1.5 TIKI / skeletor
- `skeletor/*` and `tiki/*` are compiled into the client and server only. The renderer compiles just `tiki/tiki_mesh.cpp` (bone/morph caches) and reaches the rest through `ri.TIKI_*`/`ri.SKEL_*`.
- Skinning is all on the CPU: `R_AddSkelSurfaces` (`tr_model.cpp:720`) → `ri.GetFrameInternal` → `skeletor_c::GetFrame` → bone matrices in `skelBoneCache_t` → `RB_SkelMesh` (`tr_model.cpp:1022`) skins into `tess.xyz/normal` in the backend. Vertices are variable-length (`skeletorVertex_t` + morphs + weights, no fixed cap on weights). Normals use the first bone only. `TIKI_MAX_BONES` 100, `TIKI_MAX_VERTEXES` 1000. LOD uses progressive-mesh collapse maps.

### 1.6 SDL, input, audio
- SDL2 only (2.32.8). Video and window in the renderer. Input in the client (`sdl/sdl_input.c`: keyboard, text input, relative mouse + grab, joystick/gamecontroller, window events, DROPFILE for the `openmohaa://` URL). Colour cursor in `sdl_mouse.c`. Clipboard. `sdl_snd.c` is not compiled (audio doesn't use SDL). No HiDPI support (`SDL_WINDOW_ALLOW_HIGHDPI` unused, no `NSHighResolutionCapable`).
- Audio: the active system is the MOHAA `*_new.cpp` one on OpenAL only (`NO_MODERN_DMA` undefined); there is no fallback. 3D positional sources, 16-buffer streaming for music/dialog/movies (polled, no thread), ALC_SOFT HRTF/limiter/resampler extensions. EFX reverb is a FIXME no-op. About 7.1k lines of ioq3 sound code are present but not compiled.

### 1.7 Other platforms
- Windows only: `sys/sys_win32.c`, `con_win32.c`, `sys/new/sys_win32_new.c`, .rc/manifest. `win_bounds.cpp` and `win_localization.cpp` are built everywhere despite their names. `asm/` is x86 only and not built on clang. `null/` is used by the dedicated server. `Launcher/` doesn't work on macOS. `sys_osx.m` has only `Sys_Dialog` (NSAlert) and `Sys_StripAppBundle`; it imports Carbon without using it, and IOKit is linked but unused. gamespy is 178k lines (only common/gcdkey/natneg/qr2 are built). Platform `#ifdef` density is low. **Phase 7a (session 15) deleted all of these except `null/`** (Phase 7, "Session 15 result"); the platform `#ifdef`s inside shared files stay.

### 1.8 Ideas from the user's Vulkan port (pstngh/openmohaa-vulkan, branch `vulkan-renderer`; ideas only, no code copied)
- `code/renderervk` is a copy of renderergl1 with every GL call replaced by a GL-free backend API that mirrors GL1's fixed-function state (`GLS_*` bits, texenv, cull, depth range, polygon offset, fog, clip plane, stencil, matrices, viewport/scissor, draw/clear/readback, texture create/upload/destroy). With that, the `tr_*` code barely changes and upstream renderer fixes keep porting. They added an immediate-mode emulator (`tr_immediate.c`), GPU static geometry and GPU skinning.
- Outside the renderer they changed only CMake (new renderer target, jpeg/freetype guards, macos.cmake bundle placement), `tr_common.h` (skip qgl.h, `texnum` → `unsigned int`), the `cl_renderer` default, and a new `sdl_vkimp.c` window file. The refexport/refimport ABI is unchanged.
- Gotchas they recorded:
  - Hidden visibility (only `GetRefAPI` exported) was their biggest single CPU win.
  - Keep GL projection matrices and remap clip z; mind the bottom-left window origin for viewport/scissor/readback; keep CCW front faces.
  - Reproduce the exact alpha-test thresholds, "no destination alpha" (RGB textures sample alpha = 1), Mesa-style fog, clamping stencil ops.
  - Never reuse texture handles while frames are in flight. Uploads mid-frame (cinematics, ghosts) must not change already recorded draws. Free GPU objects only after the frame's fence.
  - Frames start lazily (2D exports flush render commands). Take screenshots at end of frame (GL1 read a stale back buffer).
  - Capability flags come from the same `r_ext_*` cvars so shader collapsing matches. A default stencil of 0 bits disables `r_shadows 2`.
  - Deterministic screenshot testing: `devmap`, `fixedtime 16`, `thereisnomonkey 1`, `tele`/`face`, `pause` before `screenshot`; delete `main/configs` between runs; GL1 sometimes saves an all-black frame.

## 2. Baseline (upstream GL1, a2f34019 + the timedemo work metric)

Machine: Mac mini M4 (4P+6E, 10-core GPU, 16 GB), macOS 26.6.2, Xcode 27.1. Display: DELL G2524H 1920×1080 @ 240 Hz (main) + DELL U4323QE 4K at 2× (second).

**Build** (`port/build.sh gl`): Release, ThinLTO, universal arm64+x86_64 (forced by macos.cmake), deployment target 11.0. 85 s on 10 cores. GL context reports "2.1 Metal - 90.5": Apple's GL runs on Metal internally.

**arm64-only rebuild** (session 2, after Phase 1 set arm64 + macOS 26.0): build 36 s. Same bench, same binary, two sets: 937.1 / 941.1 / 941.1 fps = **0.896 / 0.895 / 0.893 ms work**, and later 909.4 / 925.5 / 912.5 fps = 0.954 / 0.922 / 0.941 ms. GL1 from the combined `metal` install (`cl_renderer opengl1`): 0.901 / 0.943 / 0.940 ms. So the arm64-only GL1 reference is **~0.90–0.95 ms work/frame**; between sets the noise is about ±3% (within a set ±0.3%), larger than session 1 measured. Compare against GL1 runs made in the same sitting.

**Benchmark** (`port/bench.sh run gl 3`): timedemo of `port/bench/bench_mohdm6.dm_8` (dm/mohdm6 Stalingrad, FFA, 8 bots, spectator following bots, 120 s, 2398 frames; sha256 `c62f7972735b60c15b32392168f41235849407b637c9ac6004d68a36312320a2`), 1280×720 window on the main display, `r_swapInterval 0`, `com_maxfps 0`, sound muted, fresh default config each run.

| Config | fps (3 runs) | wall ms/frame | **work ms/frame** | GPU ms/frame (`trace`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GL1 `r_primitives 2` (**reference**: the user's setting, GL's fastest path) | 923.4 / 925.9 / 926.2 | 1.081 | **0.934** (limiter wait 0.146) | **0.18** (16% GPU utilization in the timedemo) |
| GL1 `r_primitives 0` (upstream default) | 293.2 / 296.3 / 295.9 | 3.39 | 3.39 | ~0.6 (older estimate method) |

- **"work" is new.** The engine never runs a frame shorter than 1 ms: since Quake 3, `Com_Frame` pads frames to its 1 ms minimum with an integer-ms clock. So fps saturates near 1000 (with `com_maxfps 0` or in a timedemo; `com_maxfps` above 1000 removes the floor but makes the game clock run fast, see §4b rule 7), and GL with `r_primitives 2` already sits there. The timedemo now also prints `timedemo work: X ms/frame` (wall time minus Com_Frame's frame-limiter wait, µs clock; `qcommon/common.c` `com_timedemoWaitUsec`, printed in `client/cl_main.cpp CL_DemoCompleted`). **Compare renderers on work ms/frame.** It only measures; it changes nothing in how frames run.
- Run-to-run noise: ±0.3% for `r_primitives 2` and ~3% for `r_primitives 0` (one set gave 286–294 fps). Under `sample` the run is ~4% slower, under xctrace ~5–10% slower.
- **Where the GL time goes** (`sample` profiles; `port/sample_by_library.py`):
  - `r_primitives 2`: the frame is dominated by `RB_SwapBuffers`. It calls `qglFinish()` every frame (`tr_backend.c:1429`), and the CPU blocks in `GLDShareGroupRec::waitUsage` until the GPU is done, then `CGLFlushDrawable` presents. The GPU is busy only 0.18 ms of each ~1 ms frame, so most of the frame is CPU↔GPU **synchronization latency**, not rendering. The engine's own CPU work is small.
  - `r_primitives 0`: ~1.96 ms/frame in `RB_SwapBuffers` (≈half glFinish wait, half present) and ~1.7 ms/frame drawing the 3D view/HUD (`UIWindowManager::UpdateViews`). Of the latter, ~65% is Apple's GL driver (AGX, AppleMetalOpenGLRenderer, GLEngine, malloc churn from immediate mode) and ~13% renderer code (top: `RB_Light_Real` 4.7%, `RB_SkelMesh` 2.4%, `R_DrawStripElements` 1.3%).
  - Apple's GL splits every game frame into ~8–10 GPU submissions (render passes): 23806 trace frames for ~2400 game frames. On a tile-based GPU each extra pass costs tile loads/stores.
- **Metal, Phase 1** (session 2; draws are still stubs, so this is the floor of front end + backend frame overhead, not comparable with GL1): `port/bench.sh run metal 1 +set cl_renderer metal`: 998.8 fps, **0.318 ms work/frame**, no wait for drawables or GPU. With `r_swapInterval 1`: 239.1 fps, the ~3.5 ms vsync wait sits at the end of the frame (before the next input sample).
- **Metal, Phase 2a** (session 3, 2026-10-17; the whole renderer now draws, see Phase 2's result). Same sitting, `port/bench.sh run gl 3` and `port/bench.sh run metal 3 +set cl_renderer metal`, **with the screen locked** (`CGSSessionScreenIsLocked`: nothing is composited, so GL1's swap is cheaper than in §2's table and Metal gets a drawable for only ~1 frame in 15; re-measure both unlocked):

  | Config | fps (3 runs) | **work ms/frame** | GPU ms/frame |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | GL1 `r_primitives 2` | 975.2 / 982.0 / 981.2 | **0.766 / 0.759 / 0.765** | (no trace) |
  | Metal, 2 frames in flight (default) | 1000.0 / 1000.0 / 1000.0 | **0.359 / 0.364 / 0.361** | 0.11 (frame command buffer GPU time, `r_metalPresentStats 1`) |
  | Metal, `r_metalFramesInFlight 1` | 998.3 | 0.707 (0.31 ms/frame waiting for the GPU, after the commit) | |
  | Metal, `r_metalFramesInFlight 3` | 1000.0 | 0.361 | |

  - **2.1× less work per frame than GL1, under the Phase 2 target (≤ 0.45 ms).** fps is pinned at the engine's 1 ms floor.
  - CPU profile (`sample`, 8 s of real-time demo playback): 74% `select` + 7.6% `mach_absolute_time` = the engine's frame limiter polling. Of the busy time: renderer front end ≈ 9% of all samples (`RB_SkelMesh` 2.7%, `RB_Light_Real` 1.9%, `RB_SurfaceFace` 0.8%), Metal driver (AGX + IOGPU) ≈ 2%, ring copies (`memmove`) 0.9%, the backend's own functions ≈ 0.2%. GL1 spent ~65% of its busy time in Apple's GL driver.
  - Two measured traps, both fixed (see §3.2 "Added in session 3"): with the present in the frame's command buffer, completion came only at the display's next refresh while the screen was locked (runs 1 and 3 ran at 239 fps, 3.2 ms/frame waiting for a frame slot); and completed handlers arrived ~1.3 ms after the GPU had finished (0.97 ms work). Frame completion now comes from an `MTLSharedEvent`.
- **Metal, Phase 2b** (session 4, 2026-10-17, **screen unlocked**: `CGSSessionScreenIsLocked` absent before and after). Same sitting, `port/bench.sh run gl 3` and `port/bench.sh run metal 3 +set cl_renderer metal +set r_metalPresentStats 1`, then one run each with `+set r_swapInterval 1`:

  | Config | fps | **work ms/frame** | notes |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | GL1 `r_primitives 2` | 902.2 / 938.2 / 943.4 | **0.955 / 0.887 / 0.884** | |
  | Metal (2 frames in flight, 2 drawables) | 999.2 / 997.9 / 997.5 | **0.393 / 0.396 / 0.389** | GPU 0.12 ms/frame; 58 draws, 1 pass, 143 KB ring per frame; 12 pipelines; ~40% of frames get a drawable (the compositor shows ~240/s), the rest skip their present without waiting; every presented frame was shown |
  | GL1, `r_swapInterval 1` | 239.5 | (4.173: includes the vsync wait) | |
  | Metal, `r_swapInterval 1` | 237.0 | (4.218: includes the vsync wait) | 3.47 ms/frame waiting in `nextDrawable`, at the end of the frame (§4b rule 1); every frame presented and shown |

  - **2.3× less work per frame than GL1 with the compositor running**, under the Phase 2 target (≤ 0.45 ms). Metal's 0.39 ms vs 0.36 ms on a locked screen (session 3) is the cost of really getting and presenting drawables.
  - 4K@2× (U4323QE, `+set r_displayIndex 1`, 1280×720-point window): Metal draws 2560×1440 pixels, GPU 1.2 ms/frame (not benchmarked; the display runs at 60 Hz). GL1 renders the same window at 1280×720 and lets macOS upscale it.
- **Metal, Phase 2c** (session 5, 2026-10-17, screen unlocked). Bench in the same sitting (`port/bench.sh run gl 3`, `port/bench.sh run metal 3 +set cl_renderer metal`): GL1 **1.082 / 1.087 / 1.091 ms** work (GL1 ran ~15% slower than in session 4 this sitting), Metal **0.412 / 0.403 / 0.397** and 0.397 / 0.398 ms.   - **The probe's present times are real.** `TRACE=1 LATSTATS=2 port/latency.sh …` records Instruments' Metal System Trace during the run, and `port/display_trace.py` matches every present time the probe reported against the display's own swap log. Window: 1557 of 1561 present times fall within ±1 µs on a display swap that shows that very frame. Fullscreen at ~1000 fps: 2392 of 2396.
  - **A composited window costs about two refreshes, in two modes.** At 250 fps, commit → present sits at either ~5 ms or ~9.7 ms (one 240 Hz refresh apart) for stretches of 0.5–5 s, then switches (the probe's time series; Instruments agrees). At ~1000 fps the median falls to 5.1 ms: only frames that find a ready drawable are presented, and they arrive just after the compositor released the previous drawable. Phase 5: find what selects the mode (present timing, drawable count, `CAMetalDisplayLink`).
  - **Fullscreen is not direct-to-display, in either renderer.** Instruments: Metal's fullscreen layer "cannot go direct to display due to layer requires a potential offscreen render"; GL1's fullscreen surface isn't direct either. So fullscreen goes through the compositor like a window (Phase 3).
  - **Fullscreen with vsync off: Core Animation's present feedback is wrong.** Share of presented drawables reported as never shown (presented-handler status 3; `presentedTime` 0):
    - 98–99% at 250 fps;
    - ~33% at ~1000 fps;
    - almost all at 200 and 125 fps.

    Yet Instruments shows the display swapping game frames 220–240 times a second. Where Core Animation does give a time, it's right. So the probe leaves its present lines out when more than half of the presented frames are reported as never shown (fullscreen 250 fps above). In fullscreen at ~1000 fps, pump → present is an upper bound: the input of a frame reported as never shown is credited to the next frame that has a time. Re-check once fullscreen goes direct.
  - **Vsync on queues a frame.** Fullscreen at 250 fps with vsync: 11.9 ms, constant (2 drawables: each frame waits a refresh behind the one on screen). Window with vsync: 7.7 ms p50. With vsync on, the GPU also finishes 1.8 ms after the commit, against ~0.45 ms without vsync (not explained yet). Phase 5's low-latency vsync (1 frame in flight, `CAMetalDisplayLink`, just-in-time frame start) targeted both (*dropped by the user in session 63, §3.1 #37*).
  - **Commit → GPU done takes 0.35–0.45 ms** for ~0.12 ms of GPU work: the GPU starts ~0.3 ms after the commit (session 3 measured the same). So Metal's GPU done (0.75 ms p50 in a window) lands where GL1's EndFrame returns (0.68 ms, after its glFinish), although Metal commits at 0.31 ms. The submission gap is a Phase 5 target.
  - **event → pump** is the OS-side wait plus SDL's pump: ~0–2 ms for 1000 Hz events at 250 fps. The oldest and newest event of a pump are almost always the same: macOS coalesces mouse moves into one event per pump.
  - Caveat: on the local server, `SV_Frame` (the 20 Hz game frame) runs between the input pump and the usercmd on about 1 frame in 12 at 250 fps. Online clients don't do that work, so it can only inflate pump → commit's p95/p99.

  - **The cause:** the WindowServer holds our direct-to-display flip while it handles another application's frame on the other display. With the Claude app visible, the frame's GPU work is unchanged (commit → GPU start 0.39 / 0.47 ms p50 / p95, GPU work 0.40 / 0.47) but **GPU done → on screen goes from 1.08 / 1.31 ms (covered) to 1.16 / 3.81 ms**. With 2 drawables the next frame's drawable is the one still on screen until that late flip (it comes back 0.24–0.33 ms after its successor is on screen, in every run), so ~13% of frames find none and are skipped, and their input waits for the next frame (p95 ~6 ms). It isn't the 4K's composite as such (`busy` and `small` composite at 60/s and lose 0.6%) but the other application's GPU-rendered frames (the Claude app is Chromium; `gpu20` reproduces it, with GPU contention on top: our GPU work p95 4.6 ms). Game Mode was on in every exclusive run (gamepolicyd).
  - **Why the Space never lost frames:** this Mac has "Displays have separate Spaces" off (`defaults read com.apple.spaces spans-displays` = 1), so a fullscreen Space blanks the other display and the Claude app there stops drawing (session 23's Space runs: the 4K never swapped). In exclusive and the borderless window the 4K swapped 60/s in every traced run. Session 25's wider Space spread (p95 3.8–6.0 ms while the user was active) is not explained by this; see §6.
  - **3 drawables don't fix it:** every frame gets a drawable, but the flips still queue behind the late one (p95 4.6–4.9 ms), and when nothing is in the way they cost ~0.6 ms (p50 1.85 → 2.44; commit → GPU start 0.37 → 0.65 ms and GPU work 0.40 → 0.50: the GPU apparently clocked lower with more slack), as session 6 found; one Space run with 3 had p95 11.5 ms.
  - **Late presents (the fix, §3.2 "Added in session 26"):** a frame that ends without a drawable hands its final pass to the drawable thread, which presents it as soon as a drawable comes back. Its drawable came 0.34–0.47 ms (p50) and 1.6–3.1 ms (p95) after the frame's end, and a late present takes ~1.7 ms from its commit to the screen. **Every frame is now shown, and p95 drops from ~6.0 to ~4.2 ms** (p99 ~6.6 → ~4.7) in exclusive fullscreen and the borderless window while another application draws on the other display; nothing changes when nothing is in the way. The rest of the p95 is the late flip itself, which only the WindowServer controls (the Space avoids it by blanking the other display). A first version without a deadline was worse at 1000 fps (exclusive 2.50 / 2.90 → 3.76 / 5.81 ms; the window 5.34 → 6.35 p50): there the next frame is 1 ms away, and every drawable went to an older frame. With the deadline (a late present only if it can be committed 2 ms before the next frame's end) nothing is posted at 500 fps and above, and 1000 fps matches no late presents.
  - **Traced** (`LATSTATS=2 TRACE=1`, exclusive, the Claude app swapping the 4K at 60/s): the G2524H swapped 248 times a second (217 before), direct on every swap, every presented handler with a time; 1683 of the probe's 1689 present times inside the trace sit on a swap within 2 µs, 1679 showing that very frame; 36 of 4748 frames weren't presented. So the probe gets the late frames' present times, and they are real.

- **The decoupled mode's slow frames, and the render rate by the input's age on screen** (session 32, 2026-10-19, §4b part 2's follow-up; Phase 5 "Session 32 result"; the user's OK for the synthetic mouse, then away; the Space, 1920×1080 at 240 Hz, vsync off, `cl_cmdRate 125`, `cl_cmdDisplay 1`; every frame on a performance core in every run that logged them).
  - **The tail was the mode, not the instrumentation:** on the plain `metal` build the mode at render 250 still read pump → commit 0.22 / 0.56 / 0.58 and 0.20 / 0.55 / 0.57 against stock 250's 0.19 / 0.25 / 0.31 and 0.20 / 0.25 / 0.29. A scratch frame log with the frame's sections (`s32x`: IN_Frame, both event loops, `SV_Frame`, `CL_SendCmd`, BeginFrame, `CG_DrawActiveFrame`, the 2D, EndFrame) put all of it in cgame: `CG_DrawActiveFrame` ~400 µs instead of ~70 in 29–32% of the drawn frames, all in one block from the end of the loading screen to ~10 s later, while the in-process server took every packet and ran none of its usercmds (`SV_ClientThink` 0 times in 1566 of 1580 slow frames). So the snapshots' `commandTime` stood still and cgame's prediction replayed up to 64 usercmds every frame.
  - **Why:** the mode ran while the client was primed, before the first snapshot, when `cl.serverTimeDelta` is still 0. The usercmd made then stamped the next one with `cls.realtime` (10210 ms, the client's uptime) where the server's clock read 500; the loading screen paused the game, and the first usercmd after it took the client's real time (700): a step back of 9510 ms. A usercmd's time is sent as an 8-bit step from the one before when that step is below 256 (`MSG_WriteDeltaUsercmdKey`), and a step back is too, so the server read 10210 + 218 = 10428, kept it as its last usercmd and dropped every usercmd stamped below it, ~10 s of them. Online the same happens to a client whose uptime at the connection is ahead of a server's clock (a freshly started server): the player can't move for the difference.
  - **Fixed** (§3.2 "Added in session 32"): the mode starts with the first snapshot (`CA_ACTIVE`), and the next usercmd's time is never below the one before it (stock's "time never flows backwards"). After: pump → commit 0.19 / 0.23 / 0.28 against stock's 0.20 / 0.25 / 0.28; drawn work p50 / p99 199 / 279 µs (stock 208 / 290), no frame ≥ 400 µs; the server runs every usercmd from the first one.

  - **The prepass doesn't pay here** (the item asked in session 30: "will u test #3 to see if its worth it too?"). The prototype (`r_s34prepass 1`, JayRewd's form: per alpha-tested, depth-writing batch, first depth only with the alpha test, then shaded with depth EQUAL, no depth writes and no discard) costs mohdm5 +11–15% GPU time at 960 and −4 to −11% frames/s uncapped, obj_team2 +8–9% / −3 to −6%, and gains only on obj_team1 uncapped (+0–11%, the two-texture cards), ±4% there at 960. MOHAA's foliage shaders are one texture times the vertex color: the depth pass samples the same texture for every layer that the shaded pass did, so it saves only a multiply and the fog and adds a second pass. A whole-frame prepass has the same depth pass (every layer's alpha must be sampled before its depth is known), so it can save no more than the per-draw one; not prototyped.
  - **What does pay: the alpha-tested surfaces after the opaque ones** (`r_s34ftb 3`: after the sort, a stable partition of the `SS_OPAQUE` range puts every surface whose shader has an alpha-tested, depth-writing stage after the others; GL1's order is by shader, so the trees came before the terrain and the park's walls). Apple's GPUs drop hidden opaque fragments before shading, but an alpha-tested fragment is shaded before its depth is known, so trees drawn before what hides them were shaded whole. Drawn last, the finished opaque depth rejects their hidden fragments before shading. mohdm5 −8 to −26% GPU time at 960, uncapped +0 to +20% frames/s; obj_team2 uncapped +0 to +7%, at 960 −4% to +14% (0.346 → 0.396 in a view where the GPU is 35% busy and its clock governor sets the time); obj_team1 (measured with `r_s34ftb 2`), mohdm4 and m2l1 within ±4% at 960 and ±2% uncapped; slower uncapped in no view. Static models front to back within each shader (`r_s34ftb 1`) adds −1.5 to −4% on mohdm5, nothing elsewhere.

- **The draw surfaces' sort by runs of equal keys** (session 36, 2026-10-19; Phase 5 "Session 36 result", §3.2 "Added in session 36"; the user at the machine at the start (HIDIdleTime 1.7–20 s), "Later, not now" to the online test, the runs that take the cursor OK'd; unlocked throughout). Measured first with a scratch flavor `s36x` (`build.noindex/s36/`: b7f1729e's `R_RadixSort` kept beside the new one, `r_s36sort` 0 / 1 per segment, `r_s36check 1` sorting a copy with the old one too and comparing the bytes; per frame the sorts' µs, the surfaces, the key bytes that vary, the core and the frame's work, i.e. `Com_Frame` from the end of its wait to the next wait), session 35's setup and views (the Space at 1920×1080, the decoupled mode at 960, `noclip`), A B A B per view (1 s to settle, 2 s each), and each view's sort input dumped once (`r_s36keys`) for an offline benchmark of variants (`sortbench.c`, every variant checked against the old order).
  - **What the sort gets:** one `R_SortDrawSurfs` a frame on these views (no portals or mirrors), sprites only on m2l1 (0–18). The surfaces come in runs of equal keys in their input order (a BSP leaf's or a model's surfaces with one shader) and a frame has only a few hundred distinct keys: mohdm5 4,600–4,900 surfaces in 370–606 runs (8–13 a run, 260–310 distinct keys), mohdm4 1,900–3,500 in 830–1,750 (~2 a run), obj_team2 300–760 (1.6–2.3), obj_team1 57–307 (1.2–1.7), m2l1 310–1,260 (1.5). The key bits that vary are `0x3ff3ff00` on every map (the entity's low 10 bits, the static flag, 9 bits of the shader's sorted index): the dlight byte is constant, so the old sort ran three 8-bit passes. On the bench (mohdm6, 1280×720) 646 surfaces a frame (max 1,794) and 10 sprites, and all four bytes vary (dynamic lights).
  - **Why it was slow:** ~8.5 ns a surface (mohdm5 ~40 µs for 4,700), against ~2.4 ns offline on random keys of the same count. In a counting pass, neighbours that share a digit chain the counter's load, increment and store through memory, and here they nearly always do. Sorting 8-byte (key, index) pairs per surface (the brief's first idea) keeps the chain: offline 48 µs on mohdm5's input against the old sort's 32 (34 with 11-bit digits).
  - **The fix:** sort the runs instead (§3.2 "Added in session 36"). Offline on the dumped inputs: mohdm5 19–32 → 3.4–6.8 µs, mohdm4 12–21 → 6–11, the obj maps and m2l1 +3 to −40%; the same inputs shuffled (fewer runs) mohdm5 15–34 → 8–13; small inputs (4–64 surfaces) equal, 256–1,024 random or sprite-like keys +28–57% (up to +1.4 µs); all-distinct random keys +25–50% (9.6 → 12.5 µs at 4,096), an input this key layout doesn't produce (a few hundred distinct keys a frame).

- **The off-screen skeletal models** (session 37, 2026-10-19; Phase 5 "Session 37 result", §3.2 "Added in session 37"; JayRewd's b26d8a67 idea, re-implemented; the user away at the start (HIDIdleTime 2 → 570 s), back at 15:51: "Later, not now" to the online test, the runs that take the cursor OK'd; unlocked throughout). GL1's `R_AddSkelSurfaces` computed every skeletal model's frame (`R_GetFrame`: every bone's transform), copied its bones and morphs and added its surfaces even when the radius cull said `CULL_OUT` (the cull only fed the counters), and the backend then built and skinned those surfaces for the GPU to clip. Measured first with a scratch flavor `s37x` (`build.noindex/s37/`: the tree's skip behind `r_s37skip` (0 = GL1's path), `r_s37alt 1` alternating the two paths frame by frame for a paired A/B on neighbouring frames, per frame the models by class, `R_AddSkelSurfaces`' µs, the surfaces they add, the core and the frame's work; `r_s37check 1` runs GL1's path, then skins every model's vertexes on the CPU (a copy of `RB_SkelMeshVertexes`, morphs included) and tests them against the view: how far past the cull sphere they reach, and any culled model with a vertex in view).
  - **What gets culled:** on the bench (mohdm6, the spectator following 8 bots) 17.5 skeletal models a frame (players, their weapons, items), 9.1 of them outside a side plane even with the margin (9.5 by the radius alone), adding 34.9 of the frame's 69.2 skeletal draw surfaces. Live with 8 bots at 960: mohdm6 10.1 of 19, mohdm4 19.3 of 33.7, obj_team2 7.5 of 11.7; single player from the map's start: m1l1 12–28 of 34–46 (soldiers), m3l1a 6–21 of 41 (the landing craft's crews). By the far plane alone only on m3l1a yaw 90 (4 a frame; not skipped, below). No personal models (`RF_THIRD_PERSON` in the main view) on any of these views (spectator or single player), so they got no case of their own.
  - **The radius isn't strictly conservative:** the animation's radius (the skeletor's `m_frameRadius`, the largest of the blended frames' radii from the animation files) doesn't cover what the bone controllers (the aiming torso, the head) and the blends do. The vertexes reach up to 6.5 units past it (german_afrika_private on m1l1, 7.6% of its 85; the coxswain 5.6; the multiplayer players ≤ 4.2), and a muzzle flash 3.5 past its 2.6 radius (its whole extent 6.1 units); the vehicles stay 2 to 313 units inside it (jeeps, trucks, the King Tiger, the train). So the skip uses the radius × 1.1 + 16: 2.5× the largest overshoot on the soldiers, 4.5× on the flash, and the relative part keeps a scaled-up character covered. **The check over 140,000 frames** (the bench, the three bot maps, 17 single-player maps' starts in four directions with their AI, vehicles, boats and the train): **3.3 million model checks, no culled model with a vertex in view.**
  - **Not skipped:** a model past the far plane alone (GL1 draws it fogged; whether that shows depends on the fog's saturation, the sky behind it and `r_farplane_nofog`, while the side planes are geometry alone), and one whose radius is the skeletor's 2 for no animation (then the radius says nothing about its size; in the retail scenes only a dummy, m1l1truckride.tik).
  - **What else reads the bones** (checked): the backend's skinning (`RB_SkelMeshVertexes` and the GPU jobs) reads `TIKI_Skel_Bones[bonestart]` only for drawn surfaces; tags (`RE_TIKI_Orientation`, `RE_TIKI_IsOnGround`), the radius and cgame's attachments (`R_GetRenderEntity` and the parent's tag) go through the skeletor, before the scene is rendered; `parentEntity` is read only for lighting (the grid color cached along the chain, computed from the root's lighting origin by whichever member draws first: the same value); the skeletor's bones keep no state across frames (IK, AvRot, HoseRot recompute from the pose), so a model looks the same when it comes back into view; shadows are cgame's blobs and foot shadows (through the skeletor), and the renderer never adds a model shadow-volume surface (`tr.shadowShader` has no front-end user); portals and mirrors cull with their own frustum, and a view that skips a model leaves its `bonestart` at the view that drew it (a frame's bones are the same in every view); the sky portal culls its sky entities with its camera's frustum; the LOD (`lodpercentage`) is still computed for a skipped model. A scene resetting the bone cache before the previous scene's backend ran (where a shift of the bone indexes could matter): 0 in every run.
  - **In the game, paired frames** (`r_s37alt 1`; the bench: one timedemo, uncapped, 1280×720 window; the rest at 960 in the Space at 1920×1080, the decoupled mode, 8 s per bot view and 4 s per single-player view; the main thread on a performance core in ≥ 99.9% of the frames; "skeletal surfaces" = the draw surfaces `R_AddSkelSurfaces` adds a frame):

  - **Why the bots' shadows never hit at ≤ 1,000 frames a second:** cgame's clock is whole milliseconds, so at 960 almost every frame interpolates the entities to a new millisecond, and a player's feet (`CG_CastSimpleFeetShadow` places the shadow between the foot tags) move with the animation; a mark repeats only for what rests (single player's soldiers, the player standing) or above 1,000 frames a second (frames inside one millisecond). A miss costs ≤ ~17 ns (the key's hash and compare and the entry's copy).
  - **The renderer instead of the cgame for the marks:** JayRewd kept the blob shadows' final vertexes in the cgame for one server snapshot. Here `R_MarkFragments` keeps its own answer: its inputs (the polygon's points, the projection, the buffers' sizes, the radius) and `ter_minMarkRadius` are the key, and only the renderer can clear it when the terrain's heights change (`ter_crater`, `ter_restart`) or a world loads; every caller gains (blob shadows, tread marks, the permanent marks' first projection), the brush entities' fragments are still computed every call (`CG_GetMarkFragments`), and a snapshot's lifetime would have kept nothing in the timedemo. What the cgame still does per mark (the axis, the bounds, the brush entities, the per-poly callback) is ~0.3–0.6 µs.
  - **Exactness:** `r_s41check 1` in every scene of both rounds and a checked bench run: 0 differences for all five (the fragments' and points' bytes, the trace's bytes, the light's floats, no skipped terrain patch that would have done something). **The image:** `port/shot.sh regress base-s35` on the tree's `metal`: 62 of 90 captures identical, the other 28 the views that vary from run to run (dm6 view 8, dm5's snow, dm6fx views 4–7, m2l1 view 0); HEAD's `metalref` the same day: 60 identical, the same views differing (m2l1 view 0 by 12–13 pixels; the tree's two runs 10 and 8). `base-s35` stays the baseline.

A frag grenade's explosion is lit for ~12 frames only. With 8 bots at most **4 lights at once** (mohdm6, mohdm4, obj_team2, obj_team3): more than 32 never happens outside `cg_acidtrip`, so **the 64-light masks buy nothing** (not taken). Lights are on in 12% (mohdm6), 20% (mohdm4), 39% (obj_team3) of the bot maps' frames, ~0% on obj_team2, and in 33% of the frames while the player fires.
  - **What MOHAA's path costs** (HEAD as the scratch flavor `s42h`, `build.noindex/s42/inst42.py`; 960 frames a second in the Space at 1920×1080, the decoupled mode at 100; per frame with a light): the player's own gunfire (mohdm6's stair hall) 28.6 µs (`R_RealDlightFace` 26.6: 131 faces tested, 31 lit, 2,678 texels; the upload 2.0); mohdm6 / mohdm4 / obj_team3 with 8 bots 55.6 / 23.6 / 36.3 µs (the per-face test of every visible lightmapped face against every light, ~300–1,000 faces, plus the texel loops of the faces whose plane a light reaches); 8 random lights 38.1 µs, 31 lights ~112 µs. **On obj_team3 the terrain walks all 15 dlight pages:** `R_AllocLMBlock` can never place a 129-texel terrain block (its search runs `i < LIGHTMAP_SIZE - w`), so every terrain patch near a light uploads each page in turn and gets none: 12.6 µs of uploads a lit frame for nothing. (*Corrected in session 43:* not the terrain, whose blocks are all 17 texels: every one of the 26,110 terrain patches in the 140 retail maps has lmapScale 2. It is obj_team3's seven planar faces with 128-texel-wide lightmaps (mohdm4 has 2, m1l1 2, obj_team2 18), which no page can hold: one near a light walks the pages to the last, and every surface lit after it that frame shares page 14.) **With exactly 32 lights the world gets none** (`(1 << 32) - 1` is 0 with arm64's 32-bit shift; `R_AddWorldSurfaces` and `R_AddTerrainSurfaces`).
  - **The per-pixel path** (the branch): the front end keeps each surface's lights as a mask (faces: plane, `r_dlightBacks` and the face's bounds, computed at load; patches: their bounds; terrain: the patch's box), with Q3's split of the lights at each BSP node plane and a box test per leaf, a surface's mask merged across the leaves and views it is seen from in a frame (a light that reaches a surface reaches one of its leaves, so nothing is missed); lit surfaces sorted apart (the sort's dlight-map field 0/1); the backend passes a batch's lights in its object space (`RB_SetDlights` → `mbDlights`, at most 32, a fragment buffer) to the stages that sample the lightmap; a dlight pipeline variant (`mb_stage_dl_vs` / `mb_stage_dl_fs`, key bit 18, precached with each lightmap stage) adds MOHAA's `375 · color · (1 − d/r)²` (scaled by the overbright factor) to the lightmap texel, skips the square root past the radius, and scales a sum past 1 back by its largest channel; lit world batches stay in the static vertex buffer. MOHAA's dlight maps go: the three `R_RealDlight*`, `R_UploadDlights`, the 15 dlight textures, the 1.5 MB copy of the lighting lump, `r_fastdlights` (−779 lines). `ProjectDlightTexture` stays for brush-model surfaces without a lightmap.

No retail shader has `surfaceparm nodlight`.

  - **Where the per-pixel GPU time goes** (the gunfire, each variant its own specialization of the dlight shader): the lit pipelines and the separate lit batches +5.5 µs; reading the position varying +34; the light math to +82; the normalization to +92; half precision no faster (+97). Lighting whole batches instead of the lit surfaces' was +6 µs more. So it is the pixels: the player's muzzle flash sits at the camera and its radius covers nearly everything on screen, ~2 million pixels at 1080p (4× at 4K), against MOHAA's ~2,700 lightmap texels on the CPU.
  - **Not taken:** per pixel wins every scene but one (−17 to −84 µs of latency a lit frame), and that one is the light a player sees most, their own shots (+48 to +59 µs). The user's rule is "it may look different if it's faster" (§3.1 #20); it isn't, for the player's own muzzle flash.
  - **What carries over** to a faster exact path (session 43): MOHAA's cost is the per-face test (~2.6 ns a face a light: ~3,000 visible lightmapped faces on mohdm4's big views, ~8 µs a light; with 32 lights 250 µs) and the texel loop (~10 ns a texel and light, its float → int conversions and per-texel normalization), plus the terrain's page walk. The branch's node and leaf culling cuts the first (but MOHAA's path computes a surface's dlight map at its first leaf, so it must collect the lit surfaces during the walk and compute them after, or the culling misses lights); the faces' bounds tighten the test; the 32-light fix and the terrain block fix are exact elsewhere. A per-texel path on the GPU (each lit face rasterized in its lightmap rectangle into a dlight page, the lights at the texel centers) would keep MOHAA's look with a GPU cost of the texels, not the pixels; more work, measure the CPU path first.

A scratch flavor `s43x` (`build.noindex/s43/inst43.py`): each item's old path behind a bit of `r_s43old` (1 no culling, 2 HEAD's `R_RealDlightFace` / `Patch` / `Terrain` and its out-of-line `R_DlightSample` verbatim, 4 HEAD's `R_AllocLMBlock`, 8 the faces' texels one by one, 16 no dlights on the world), `r_s43alt 1` = blocks of four frames new, old, old, new, `r_s43check 1` = HEAD's functions run beside the new ones; session 42's scenes at 960 frames a second in the Space at 1920×1080, the decoupled mode at 100, the main thread on a performance core in 99.9–100% of every segment's frames; HEAD's own cost re-measured the same day on session 42's `s42h`.
  - **What changed** (§3.2 "Added in session 43"): (1) **the culling:** each BSP node keeps the bounds of the dlight texels of the lightmapped faces and patches in its leafs (a face's: the positions `R_RealDlightFace` computes its texels at, summed the same way, one unit wider; a patch's: its mesh bounds, one unit wider); `R_RecursiveWorldNode` drops at each node the lights whose radius misses them, and `R_RealDlightFace` also drops a light that misses the face's own bounds (MOHAA tested the plane only). A light that reaches a texel reaches the bounds of every node above every leaf the surface is in, visible or not, so a surface gets the lights MOHAA's tests would let light a texel whichever leaf it is first seen from: the per-surface work stays where MOHAA does it, in the same order (session 42's walk split by node planes and leaf boxes depended on the visited leafs, and would have missed a light reaching a surface's texels in a leaf out of view). (2) **The texels:** `R_DlightSample` skips a light whose squared distance is past its reach ((radius × 1.0001 + 1)²) before the square root, reads a copy of its color and takes the normalization's factor from a table; a face's rows go four texels at a time (`R_DlightSample4`, NEON: the positions summed one by one as before, then each light lane by lane in MOHAA's order and rounding: `fma(z, z, fma(x, x, y·y))`, the float square root, the double (1 − add)² · 375, `fma(t, color, (float)r)` truncated, the double division past the table). (3) **The page search:** `R_AllocLMBlock` returns at once for a block no page can hold (w ≥ 128 or h > 128) and searches with `R_FindLMBlock` (the same answer, the first column of the lowest window maximum, by NEON doubling over the heights kept as bytes: 137 → 40 ns a search offline). (4) **32 lights light the world** (`(int)((1ull << n) - 1)`; §3.1 #20).

(The first runs differed on brush models: HEAD sets a brush model's `needDlights` to 0 or 1 and passes it as its faces' light bits, so only light 0 can light a door; the check had passed all the scene's lights. Kept as HEAD's.) Session 42's light views (`s42_dl6.cfg`, `s42_dl4.cfg`; 18 captures, new and old paths) identical to `s42h`'s. Offline (`build.noindex/s43/texbench.c`, `allocbench.c`): 25,000 random faces with 1–31 lights byte-identical for every variant, 800,000 searches identical.

The steps are the grid's now; the time delta's corrections (+1 ms ~13 times a second, −2 ~7 times) move the usercmds in real time instead, and the packets with them. The margin is ~8 ms less: a usercmd's time is now its window's end (the grid point the server time passed), where it was the window's start (the usercmd frame before's time); a stock client at ~1000 frames a second stamps one frame back, so the same. On a LAN the least was 3–6 ms: the time sync keeps the client's time ~5 ms behind the newest snapshot, whose time the server has reached; a ping adds the travel time.

The code: three scratch switches in `CL_SendCmd`'s mode (`code/client/cl_input.cpp`), kept on the local branch `s51-subgrid` (b85e429b, not pushed) and as `build.noindex/s51/subgrid.patch`: `s51subgrid` 0 off (today's grid), 1 a fire click (attack primary or secondary), 2 every starting event (fire, use, jump, a movement key pressed with none held at the last usercmd); `s51restart` 0 the grid goes on after the early usercmd (its 8 ms step split 4 + 4), 1 the grid starts again from it (4, then 8s); `s51timed` for movement and jump (below). A starting event seen by a frame between usercmds takes the next usercmd to the sub-grid's point, the newest usercmd's time + 4 ms (`CL_CmdGrid`'s step; `Com_Frame` starts a frame there through `CL_CmdClock`, as for the grid's points), made by the first frame at it; an event first seen by a frame whose frame before was already past that point waits for the grid; one early usercmd a grid step; the early usercmd's packet, and the split's rest's, go at once (`cl_maxpackets` would hold a usercmd 4 ms after the last packet's); the open step shows the sub-grid's step. In every run the server ran every usercmd made (the spawn's two aside, as before), only steps of 8 and 4 ms, one new usercmd a packet; the early packets 2–6 ms after the one before (at most two in a grid step). About 60% of the presses get an early usercmd (a press seen in the step's first half, or with the frame before still before the point). The usercmd made → the server ran it is ~0.03 ms (loopback); the frame that sees a press comes 0.6–1.2 ms after it at the median.
    - **Movement and jump**: their share of a usercmd's window counts in whole milliseconds from the frame that saw the key (`CL_KeyState`, stock), so a usercmd made in the press's own millisecond has no move from it (also today: forward and jump 1 ms slower than fire and use). With `s51timed` 0 an early usercmd made by the frame that saw the press carried no move, the move came in the split's rest (11 of 32 forward, 17 of 28 jump) or, with the restart, 8 ms later (jump's max 12.03, worse than off). `s51timed` 1: a movement or jump press is early only when a frame saw it before the point (the early usercmd has ≥ 1 ms of it). `s51timed` 2 also: a key pressed in the grid usercmd's own millisecond (no share of it) is still a starting event after it, so its early usercmd comes 4 ms later instead of the next grid point's 8: forward and jump then 2.9–3.1 ms at the mean and ≤ 6.4 at the most, against 5.2–5.3 and 10.0 off.
  - *The stuck rate at bump edges: a sweep* in the server game (`Player::ClientThink`, cvar `s51sweep`: the server's own `Player::ClientMove` run with made-up usercmds, forward and run at the bump's yaw, the player's state put back after) on dm/mohdm2 at the Vulkan port's bumps C1 `-2624 331 38` south, C3 `-2817 -1485 18` north, C7 `-1330 -3587 -6` north-west: starts 64–256 units before each in 2s, −12 to +12 to the side in 4s, on the floor below (679, 679 and 554 starts; 64,944 walks, 13.1 M moves in 27 s). A walk stopped = not 32 units past the bump's point within 2.5 s (the Vulkan port's measure). Step k is the short step's place against the 8 ms walk's step reaching the point (r = k − nref):

    | bump | every step 8 ms | every step 4 ms | split (4 + 4) at r = −6…+4 | split, by r | restart (4, then 8s) at r = −6…+4 | restart, by r | first step short (k = 0): split / restart | far before (k = 1, 5, 10, 20): split / restart |

    | C3 | 34% | 83% | 35% | 31–32% at −6…−2, 37% at −1 and 0, 41% at +1, 35–37% after | **42%** | 45–46% at −6…−1, 42 / 39 / 34% at 0 / 1 / 2 | 34% / 33% | 31% / 35% |
    | C7 | 34% | 65% | 30% | 28–29% at −6…−1, 26% at 0, 32–36% at +1…+4 | 27% | 22–25% at −6…−1, 27–33% after | 34% / 35% | 32% / 36% |

    The split leaves the walk the same (C1: 0 of 7,469 walks freed, 94 newly stopped, every one with the pair on C1's lip step, r = +1) except where the two short steps meet the edge; the restart moves every later step by half a step, so an early usercmd before a bump draws that bump's outcome again (C3: 2,105 newly stopped and 1,497 freed of 7,469), at the 8 ms odds when it is far before (k = 1–20 and 0: within 3 points of the 8 ms rate) and worse at C3 / better at C7 near the edge. Every step 4 ms, a stock client at 250 frames a second, stops far more (C3 83% against 34%), as the Vulkan port found.

- **What this means for Metal:** with frames in flight (no per-frame wait), one render pass per frame where possible, and no driver state validation, the frame cost should approach max(CPU, GPU) instead of their sum. **Phase 2 target: work ≤ 0.45 ms/frame (≥2× GL1 `r_primitives 2`) on this bench. Phase 5 stretch: ≤ 0.25 ms.** Beyond ~1000 fps the visible fps stays capped by the engine's 1 ms frame floor (see Phase 5).

---

## 3. Decisions

### 3.1 User decisions (asked in session 1, 2026-10-16)
1. **Windowing/input: SDL2 now, native later.** Phases 1–5 keep SDL2 and attach a `CAMetalLayer` via `SDL_Metal_CreateView`. Phase 6 replaces SDL with native AppKit + GameController (GCMouse raw deltas), decided after measuring input latency.
2. **Audio: keep OpenAL-soft.** *Replaced by #36 (2026-10-22): a native sound engine.* MOHAA's OpenAL sound code stays. Phase 7 bundles openal-soft in the .app, linked directly instead of dlopen'ed. A native CoreAudio/AVAudioEngine backend is only an option if profiling ever shows a reason.
3. **Platforms: macOS-only, keep the server.** Delete Windows/Linux/Emscripten/x86 asm/Launcher platform code and the GL renderers. Keep the dedicated server target (`omohaaded`) building on macOS for local tests (since session 46 only with `-DBUILD_SERVER=ON`, #30). The user's Linux servers keep using upstream builds; `main` stays the upstream mirror.
4. **Shaders: offline .metallib.** CMake compiles the hand-written `.metal` files into one metallib at build time with the read-only mounted Metal Toolchain. At run time an `MTLBinaryArchive` pipeline cache avoids compile hitches.
5. **Push: yes.** Push `metal` to origin at the end of every phase (recorded in CLAUDE.md).
6. **Lowest input latency and overhead** (asked by the user after the plan was written): a standing requirement next to the Goal. See §4b.
7. **Client timing redesign: both parts approved** (2026-10-16): precise frame pacing as the default, and an optional mode with separate command and render clocks that the user tests online before it can become the default. Planned for Phase 5 (§4b). No VRR work (the user isn't interested). Refined 2026-10-17 with the user and JayRewd (see Phase 5): exact µs caps, a selectable fallback for the movement display, a suggest-only fps cap from frame-time percentiles. The user will never use VRR and plans to cap fps (2026-10-17): the present guard is dropped, low-latency vsync moves up, and the recommended setup is recorded in Phase 5.
8. **Phase order after 5b** (2026-10-17, relayed by session 1 and recorded at session 14's hand-over), the user's words: "Yes, reorder: finish 5b, then Phase 7 (strip code, app bundle, OpenAL bundled), then Phase 6 (measure SDL latency first, then native AppKit/GameController), then the latency work, then final docs."
   - Order: 5b (done) → **Phase 7** without the README (strip the non-macOS and dead code, an arm64 `.app`, openal-soft built from pinned source and linked directly) → **Phase 6** → **the remaining Phase 5 latency work** → **final docs/README** (Phase 8).
   - Phase 6 starts by measuring SDL's input latency with the probe (the baseline), then replaces SDL with native AppKit/GameController window and input. Raw mouse via GCMouse moves into Phase 6, and the native input should give precise input timestamps for the probe. The user tests the feel at the end.
   - The latency work then runs on the final layer: precise pacing, the decoupled 125 cmd/s mode with click-time aim, the percentile cap suggestion, low-latency vsync, Game Mode/QoS, and audio latency (after Phase 7 bundles openal-soft).
   - Slice 3d (a few minutes of play in borderless fullscreen, the online smoke test) stays open and separate, whenever the user is back.
   - Amended the same day: the user moved 5c (the failed sound opens) ahead of Phase 7 ("lets do it now"), after session 14 pointed out it doesn't depend on Phases 6/7. Done in session 14.
9. **The update checker: "Disable it entirely"** (the user, 2026-10-17, asked in session 16). Compiled out in bd8c7804 (Phase 7 "Session 16, continued"). It had never run: `HAS_LIBCURL` is defined nowhere. Deleted with curl in session 22 (#16).
10. **openal-soft from source: "I approve if it's exactly what upstream does"** (the user, 2026-10-18, asked in session 16). So the download and the library are upstream's: upstream's macOS release workflow (`.github/workflows/shared-build-macos.yml` on `main`) checks out `github.com/kcat/openal-soft` at tag **1.24.3** (a lightweight tag on commit `dc7d7054a5b4f3bec1dc23a42fd616a0847af948`, 2025-03-29), builds it with openal-soft's default options (it passes only the install prefix, the architectures and verbose output), and ships `libopenal.1.dylib` beside the executable. Not the 1.25.2 tarball session 16 proposed first. Approved: fetching that tag once into `build.noindex/` and vendoring the tree. The packaging stays the user's session-1 decision (#2: inside the .app, linked directly), not upstream's (a loose dylib, dlopen'ed).
    - **Amended the same day, the version:** "Wait, but I approve the newer version, though. Don't need to use the older version." So: upstream's method (the GitHub tag, default options) with the newer release, tag **1.25.2** (a lightweight tag on commit `b2c48f7718ef3fcf67921a8b6534c4914e328970`, 2026-05-12, the latest release; the version the port has run with all along, through Homebrew). Approved: fetching that tag once into `build.noindex/` and vendoring it as `code/thirdparty/openal-soft-1.25.2`, replacing the headers-only `openal-soft-1.24.3`. Not 1.24.3.
    - **Done in session 17** (Phase 7 "Session 17 result"): the tag fetched once (commit `b2c48f77` checked), vendored whole, built by our CMake with the default options and linked directly from `Contents/Frameworks`. The differences from upstream's build, all recorded there: arm64 only, our Release flags and deployment target, no utilities/examples/install files, the Homebrew-only backends off (none was found anyway), and **one forced by this machine's SDK:** the macOS 26 SDK marks CoreAudio's render callback type `nonblocking`, and openal-soft 1.25.2's default `-Werror=function-effects` then rejects its two unannotated callback lambdas; `-Wno-error=function-effects` on the library makes them warnings again (no source change, the same code).

Isn't it better to match it one-to-one instead of, like, you know, having more?"). `cl_cmdRate` takes 85–125 (it took 85–250: 250 was the user's option of 2026-10-17, when they played stock at 250 fps), as the Vulkan port does. With `cl_maxpackets` at its 125 every usercmd has a packet of its own, and the most a player sends is a stock 125 fps client's stream. Shorter steps catch on small bumps more often: the Vulkan port's pmove sweep (b19079eb, dm/mohdm2, 29,315 walks) stalled 103 times with 4 ms steps (250 a second) against 48–66 with 8–12 ms (85–125). A config above 125 plays at 125. Code: `CL_CmdInterval`'s clamp (`code/client/cl_input.cpp`). Built and checked with glcheck; the timedemo bench doesn't run the mode (`CL_CmdInterval` is 0 in a timedemo), so it can't change; no game run. Not in the first v1.0.0 (ab81ff5b); in the v1.0.0 of session 66 (#39).

32. **`cl_cmdRate` is `cl_movefps`** (the user, 2026-10-22, session 47: asked which name is more accurate, `cl_cmdfps` (the Vulkan port's) or `cl_cmdRate`, then for a better one, they chose session 47's proposal: "We can do move FPS, and I'll change the Vulkan one as well"). Each usercmd is one step of the movement physics (pmove's frame), so `cl_movefps 125` reads as "movement at 125 steps a second", apart from the render rate; `cl_tickrate` would suggest the server's tick (`sv_fps`), and Counter-Strike's `cl_cmdrate` is a packet rate. One name for both ports once the user renames the Vulkan port's `cl_cmdfps`. No carry-over code (the user, on hearing of one: "i dont want something in teh code for that. people will just have tpo update their config"): a config's `seta cl_cmdRate` creates a cvar nothing reads, so the game plays at the default 100 until the player changes the line to `seta cl_movefps`; the README says so, and the next release notes should. `port/latency.sh` passes both names (older flavors take `cl_cmdRate`); session scripts that pass `+set cl_cmdRate` (`build.noindex/s31/svc31.sh` and the like) need `cl_movefps` for builds since. `cl_cmdDisplay` keeps its name. Code comments, the README, `INSTALL.txt` and CLAUDE.md say `cl_movefps`; this plan's history keeps `cl_cmdRate`, and `docs/RELEASE_NOTES_1.0.0.md` stayed as published until session 66 rewrote it for the second v1.0.0 (#39).
