- **What to tell the user:** (1) **Shots only, with the grid going on** (`s51subgrid 1`, the split): a click's usercmd reaches the server 2.7 ms sooner on average, 1.56 instead of 4.24 ms (worst 4.0 instead of 9.6) at your 480 / `cl_movefps 125`; about 60% of clicks get the 4 ms usercmd, the rest already fall in the step's second half. Its cost at bumps: none, except when the shot's two 4 ms steps land on the step that meets a lip: at mohdm2's C1 that one step stops 69% of runs instead of 55%; at C3 a few points more for 2–4 steps; at C7 none. A shot at a random moment of a one-second run lands its pair on that step about once in 200 runs (60% early × 1 step of 125); in the game, 142 runs into the three bumps with a shot right at the edge stopped 32% against 27% without (within the noise). notuern's "edge cases only" holds. (2) **Every starting event** (also use, jump and the first movement press): works too, the presses on average 2.3 ms sooner (all of them 2.41 against 4.74 ms, movement and jump 2.9–3.1 against 5.2–5.3), but it needed two rules for movement keys (their share of a usercmd counts in whole milliseconds from the frame that saw the key, so a usercmd made in that millisecond carries no move); more 4 ms steps (one more usercmd per press, 4 ms after the one before), the first step from standing split 4 + 4 (C1 59% stopped instead of 55%, C3 and C7 the same), and jumps' take-off steps short (not swept). (3) **Split, not restart:** restarting the grid from the early usercmd gives the same gain but moves every later step by half a step (about a unit of running), so each early shot redraws the next bump's outcome (C3 42% stopped against 34% near the edge; in the game 35% against 27%). (4) Either changes what the server receives: a usercmd 4 ms after the one before (as a stock client at 250 frames a second sends all the time), with the split one more usercmd and packet per early event, at most two packets in 8 ms; no server ran fewer usercmds in any run. **Nothing is kept until you say so**; if you want shots only, it's the patch's `s51subgrid 1` made the default (a real cvar name, the scratch ones dropped), with the checks again.
- **Recommendation:** if anything, shots only with the split: the shot's latency is what matters most (no lag compensation in MOHAA), the gain is measured and steady, and the cost is an edge case at one step of a lip. Every starting event: about the same gain for movement and jump (2.3 ms) but about four times the short steps (432 against 120 of ~22,900 in the test runs), the first step from standing split, and two extra rules for movement keys; worth trying only after shots only, if the user wants it.

Where things stood (end of session 48):
- **The freezes above ~500 frames a second** (the user's report, 2026-10-22, §6 below): **not reproduced** (§2 "The freeze hunt, and the picture at high frame rates"). At every render rate, in a window and in exclusive fullscreen, with a simulated ping, jitter, loss, bots, sound and a listen server, the local server ran every usercmd and the icon's condition never held; by the code the stamps are stock 125's and can't run ahead. The icon (`CG_DrawDisconnect`) needs more than a second in which the server runs none of the usercmds (127 back at 125 a second), which no render rate can cause here: most likely the connection then (`cg_lagometer 1` shows it next time). What the user called a freeze matched what was measured instead (told the result, they said: "it wasnt really a freeze though, its really hard to describe, just felt unstable"): **the picture's unevenness at high frame rates** (whole-millisecond time sampled at any moment: steps of 0.55–1.45 times the expected from shown frame to shown frame, uncapped and at 240) **and the partial step's stalls on bumps**, both fixed by §3.1 #33. Seen once and not again: a 0.55 s stall of the whole machine in the first exclusive-fullscreen uncapped run.
- **What the user should feel:** smooth own movement and smooth other players at any `com_maxfps`, uncapped included, no hitches on terrain, movement keys on screen sooner. **The cap to use: `com_maxfps 480`** in exclusive fullscreen (session 32: input on screen as early as 960, ~0.4 ms behind uncapped, which keeps a core and the GPU busy and is where the one stall was seen); 240 is smooth too now.
- **Matching the Vulkan port's `cl_cmdfps` later, layer by layer** (b19079eb + JayRewd's 6b9d6021; to match fully, change each "ours"):
  1. *The command clock and the stamp.* Ours: usercmds on `com_frameTime`'s clock every 1000 / rate ms rounded up (8 at 125, 10 at 100), stamped with the time delta of the usercmd frame before (stock's formula without the drawn frame's clamp, never back): steps 8 / 9 / 6 ms at 125 (the time delta's +1 / −2, as stock 125), packets exactly 8 ms apart in real time, `Com_Frame` starts each usercmd's frame on its tick. Vulkan: a usercmd when `cl.serverTime` passes the next point of a grid of server time, stamped exactly one step after the one before: steps always the interval, creation times moving with the time delta. Not taken: no measurement favours it (session 48: neither drops a usercmd; ours is a stock client's stream). Changes needed: `CL_SendCmd`'s clock and `cmd_stamp`, `CL_CmdClock` / `Com_Frame`'s usercmd tick (the grid's next point in real time), the open step's phase (the grid's).
  2. *Slow frames* (below the command rate). Ours: a usercmd due before the cap's frame gets a frame of its own that doesn't draw; one late by less than an interval is made up by the next, after a longer gap the clock restarts. Vulkan: several usercmds in one frame with the same input (up to 100 ms of them).
  3. *The display between usercmds:* the same idea now (one whole step with the keys held now, shown by the part gone). Differences: the phase (ours the client's window in µs; Vulkan's cgame (`cg.time` − the newest's time + a fraction from the first frame of each millisecond) / the cvar's interval); the step's length (ours the next usercmd's own, 6 / 8 / 9; Vulkan's always the interval, as its stamps); the turning keys under `+strafe` (projected here, not there: its look turns them every frame); the weapon command bits (ours none, Vulkan keeps the newest's); the imports (ours `GetLiveUserCmd(ucmd, &phase)` and `GetRenderTimeFraction()`; Vulkan `GetViewUserCmd`, `GetLiveUserCmd(ucmd)`, `GetRenderTimeFraction()`).
  4. *The world's render time:* ours interpolates at the frame's moment; Vulkan at whole milliseconds (its README lists the finer time as proposed).
  5. *Click-time aim:* ours gives a click's usercmd the click frame's angles and its packet that frame's eye info; Vulkan the angles of the frame that makes the usercmd.
  6. *The off switch and `cl_cmdDisplay`:* ours `cl_movefps 0` = stock and `cl_cmdDisplay` 0 / 1 / 2; Vulkan neither (85–125 only, one display).
  7. *0 ms frames:* ours count as 0 ms only in the decoupled mode (`Com_ModifyMsec`); Vulkan's at any client cap above 1000 and uncapped at timescale 1. Both guard `CG_Splash`.
  8. *Already the same:* the range 85–125 and the default 100, a sent usercmd never changes, key taps counted like stock, the view turned every frame, no packet without a new usercmd, no 1000 fps cap, the open step's idea. The name: `cl_movefps` here, `cl_cmdfps` there until the user renames it.
- **Next items (optional):** the stock time sync's +1 / −2 ms corrections smoothed for drawing only (3.8% of the shown frames uncapped; the usercmds' stamps must keep the stock delta); the extrapolated path and effects at the frame's moment; the kernel's IOSurface log lines (harmless, ~450–1070 a second with any Metal flavor). Gotchas found in session 42:
- **A light at the camera covers the screen:** per-pixel lighting costs the pixels it covers (~2 million at 1080p, 4× at 4K), per-texel lighting the lightmap texels (~2,700 for a muzzle flash). Compare GPU work by what it scales with.
- **One more float3 varying cost ~30 µs of GPU a frame over a full 1080p screen** at 960 frames a second on this M4 (the GPU at partial clocks): count varyings in a pipeline drawn over the whole screen.
- **Measure shader variants as separate specializations:** one shader holding every variant behind a uniform branch costs every variant the worst one's registers (the math skipped still cost +56 µs; specialized by a function constant, +5.5 µs).
- **The bot runs' views differ from run to run** (the spectator follows whichever bot `+use` finds): compare two flavors there by in-binary deltas (`r_s42alt`) or each item's own timer, never by the frame's work.
- **`cg_acidtrip N`** (a cheat cvar) adds N random lights in view every frame: a stress test, random, so not for screenshots (`r_s42light` gives fixed ones). With N = 32 MOHAA lights nothing (the 32-light bug).
- **A branch without switching:** `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> git read-tree HEAD; git add -u <paths>; git write-tree; git commit-tree <tree> -p HEAD; git branch <name> <commit>` saves the work tree's changes as a commit on a new branch, leaving the index, the checkout and `metal` alone (session 42's `s42-dlights-perpixel`).
- **A `cd` in a Bash call still moves the session's working directory** (three times this session): subshells or absolute paths.

Gotchas found in session 41:
- **An AskUserQuestion waits until it is answered:** asked at 22:20 with the user 24 s idle, it was answered at 06:24 (the session idle 8 hours). Ask only with the idle time at a few seconds, or start the work that needs no window first.
- **At ≤ 1,000 frames a second cgame's state is new every frame** (its clock is whole milliseconds, so entities interpolate to a new time, and a player's feet move with the animation): a cache keyed on an entity's state keeps only what rests (single player's standing soldiers, the player standing still), or the frames inside one millisecond above 1,000 frames a second.
- **The timedemo plays one snapshot a frame:** a cache that lives for one snapshot keeps nothing there; the bench can't show such a cache, m1l1's start (soldiers standing on terrain) can.
- **One mark on terrain costs ~25–29 µs** (`R_AddMarkFragmentsToTerrain` clips each patch's 128 triangles in the box): the blob shadows on terrain were m1l1's largest CPU item.
- **A `cd` in a Bash call still moves the session's working directory** (three times this session): subshells or absolute paths.

Gotchas found in session 38:
- **The screen locks at the first moment without a game window once the input has been idle ~20 minutes** (the game's `NSActivityIdleDisplaySleepDisabled` keeps it up while it runs, nothing else does; `displaysleep` is 0 here): session 38's lock came during a 90-second build between runs. Build first, then run back to back.
- **A scripted menu toggle doesn't move the cursor:** the release warps it to the window's center and the next capture finds it there, so a capture's warp never runs in such a run; `s38warp` (in `s38x` / `s38h`) moves the released cursor inside the window.
- **MOHAA has no `toggleconsole` command** (the console key calls `UI_ToggleConsole` directly); `togglemenu main` toggles the menu from a cfg.
- **The first synchronous WindowServer call of a frame pays ~0.25–0.5 ms in a window, whichever it is** (the associate went 50 → 380 µs when the warp before it was skipped), and a pump after the cursor rects' invalidation waits as long again: compare a sequence's total, not one call.
- **`lldb` can't run a test program under a locked screen** (it stopped at `run`; the debugger's authorization can't show): disassembling AppKit (in the shared cache only, no file under `/System/Library/Frameworks`) needs an unlocked session.

Gotchas found in session 32:
- **A usercmd's time is sent as an 8-bit step when it is below 256 ms ahead of the one before** (`MSG_WriteDeltaUsercmdKey`), and a step back is "below 256" too: it arrives as `from + (step & 255)`, ahead. Never let a usercmd's time go back (stock's `CL_SetCGameTime` clamp guarantees it; the mode now clamps its stamp).
- **The single-player loading screen pauses the game** (`paused 2`, `Com_FakePause`) until `finishloadingscreen`; the client is primed (`CA_PRIMED`) and makes a usercmd or two before the first snapshot, whose `cl.serverTimeDelta` is still 0.
- **The synthetic mouse at exactly 1000 Hz keeps one phase against the game's millisecond frames for a whole run** (newest event → pump 0.44 to 1.26 ms p50 from run to run): use `MOUSEHZ=997` when comparing anything that includes the event's time.
- **The per-frame latency lines can't compare render rates:** they leave out how long each image stays up (4 ms at 250, ~2 ms at 480). Use the probe's "input age on screen (by time)".
- **The frame log's first 20% isn't the probe's part:** single-player runs spend ~16 s loading and on the loading screen; `fl32.py` takes the part from 2 s after the 200th usercmd.
- **`kill -STOP` on a driver script doesn't stop the game it started:** wait for the game's PID to end, then `kill -TERM` + `-CONT` the script between runs.
- **A `cd` in a Bash call still moves the session's working directory** (twice this session): subshells or absolute paths.

Gotchas found in session 31:
- **MOHAA's playerstate `walking` (and `groundPlane`, `groundTrace`, `falldir`) isn't networked:** a predicted state with no pmove after the snapshot (every usercmd acknowledged) has `walking` 0, and the first-person model plays a landing sound when it flips (the decoupled mode on a LAN until session 31's fix).
- **The in-process input's key events are taken by the frame that made them** (`s30input` runs after `IN_Frame`, before the event loop): the click's frame is the last frame starting before the key's time, not the first after it (the first click analysis read one frame late: 0.28° at 0.29°/ms).
- **`s30input 0` turns off all of the in-process input,** keys too: keys without the mouse need a tiny mouse rate (`INPUT=0.0001`).
- **A trimmed server log can't be matched to the client's presses by order:** match over the whole log.
- **A fresh scratch install has no pak links again** (session 24's gotcha): the first `svc31.sh` run's server found 0 pk3 files; any client run of the flavor makes them.
- **The probe at render rates above the display's:** "shown by a later one" counts frames replaced before they reached the screen; at 960 about half are, uncapped three quarters.
- **`s30log` is one cvar for the client's frame log and the server's packet log:** with an in-process server (single player, the probe) `+set s30log 1` made the server write its log to `./1` in the repo root (moved to `build.noindex/s31/logs/`). Give the in-process runs a path or patch `S30_File` first.

Field 51 gives the window number but a wrong `locationInWindow`. What works (`MsPost` in `port/kbreplay.m`): `+[NSEvent mouseEventWithType:location:…windowNumber:…]` for the window and the point, its `CGEvent` copied, the type set, and the other event's fields copied over except 41, 43, 44, 50, 51, 52, 55 and 102 (found by trying); exact points, any button number, line and pixel scrolls. - **Every pk3 file lookup misses the directory search paths first** (`home.noindex/main`, then the install's `main`), so anything that costs per directory miss costs per file read.
- **A `cd` in a Bash call moves the session's working directory** in this app: use subshells or absolute paths.
- **In MOHAA the 2D draws flush the render commands** (`Draw_StretchPic` and friends call `R_IssuePendingRenderCommands`), so the 3D backend runs inside cgame's draw (`CL_CGameRendering`) and `RE_EndFrame` only presents (~5–15 µs). To time the backend, time `R_IssueRenderCommands`, not `RE_EndFrame`.
- **The timedemo frame boundary is inside `CL_SetCGameTime`, before the demo messages are read:** frame N's work includes parsing frame N's snapshot (and the sounds it starts) plus the next `Com_Frame`'s `IN_Frame`/event loop.
- **A `Com_Printf` inside a frame costs time too** (console + stdout): a temporary per-frame print adds to the next frame's work. Print only the slow frames, or buffer.
- **BSD `patch` leaves `.orig` files** when a hunk applies with an offset: `build.sh gl` passes `--no-backup-if-mismatch`.
- **`ld: warning: reducing alignment of section __DATA,__common`** is old (in session 12–13 build logs too), not from the new `clc` array.

Gotchas found in session 13:
- **The bench's first run after a build can be an outlier** (metalref 0.289 vs 0.24–0.25 after it): it showed up once in 30 runs. Look at the run list, not only the mean.
- **A cache can be faster bounded than unbounded:** the collapsed index lists ran faster with a 2 MB pool and flushes (88% reuse) than with an unbounded 32 MB one (95% reuse). Size caches by measuring, not by hit rate.
- **`sample` prints C++ frames with their parameter list** (`SCR_SimpleUpdateScreen()`), so `port/sample_by_library.py`'s subtree argument missed C++ functions; fixed in session 13 (it compares the bare name now). The frame-work total of a profile is `CL_Frame` − `CL_DemoCompleted` + `IN_Frame` samples.

Gotchas found in session 12:
- **`world_t` already has `staticModels`** (the instance array): the static-buffer offset is `staticModelVerts`.
- **Static models are drawn mostly by the generic iterator** (one stage, `rgbGen vertex`, `alphaGen vertex`), not the vertex-lit one (~1% of their surfaces). Count before assuming an iterator.
- **The skinab build step can fail on a stale anchor while the bench still runs the old metalab install:** check `skinab.sh`'s last line says "installed" before reading the SKINAB line.
- **The Bash tool refuses `sleep N; cmd` chains:** wait with a background `until …; do sleep 5; done` (run_in_background) or the Monitor tool.

Gotchas found in session 11:
- **`pgrep -f '<pattern>'` in a wait loop matches the loop's own shell** (its command line contains the pattern), so the loop never ends. Wait on a PID, a log line, or `pgrep -x openmohaa` instead. The stuck waiters from earlier sessions (`until ! pgrep -f "shot.sh regress"…`, `…"prof/pairs.sh"…`) ran until session 17, when the user asked to clean up the old sessions: two were left, both in session 10, and they kept the app from archiving it ("live work"); session 17 stopped them (`ps -Aww` shows the whole command line; plain `ps -A` cuts it).
- **Metal's "safe" math mode still contracts within an expression** (front-end `fmuladd`, like clang's `-ffp-contract=on`). So `(a.x*b.x + a.y*b.y) + a.z*b.z` compiles to the same fma chain as the explicit `fma()`s. To change the rounding, change the association. MSL `uint3` in a struct is 16-byte aligned; the A/B capture struct uses `uint[3]`.
- **Vertex functions that write a device buffer** ("writable resources in non-void vertex function") are a warning, an error under the shader build's `-Werror`: `skinab.sh` drops `-Werror` in its scratch copy only.
- **`skinSurface_t` already exists** in `tr_local.h` (Q3 skins); the GPU-skinning tables are `skinCopySurface_t`/`skinCopyBoneMap_t`.
- **`TIKI_Skel_Bones` is reset per `RE_RenderScene`** (`TIKI_Reset_Caches`), so the same pointer holds other bones in the next scene: the backend's bone copies are keyed by `backEnd.viewParms.frameSceneNum` (`mbSkinDraw_t.scene`).

Gotchas found in session 10:
- **m2l1 view 0 varies by 0–17 pixels from run to run** with the same binary (the unchanged build against itself: 1 and 17 pixels). Rerun before reading a small m2l1 difference as a change. dm6 view 8 (weapon-bar highlight), dm5 (snow) and dm6fx views 4–7 (firing, grenades) vary as before.
- **`-fno-strict-aliasing` is on for the whole build** (upstream's flags): any store through a `byte`/`float` pointer forces later loads of anything else to be redone. Copy loop-invariant data (lights, bones) to locals before hot loops; that alone is exact.
- **Exactness of restructured float loops:** clang decides FMA fusion per expression in the front end (`-ffp-contract=on`), so a loop rewritten with the same macros and expressions per element rounds the same, even when it vectorizes. Different expressions (e.g. splitting `a + b*c` into two statements) do not.
- **Profiling:** `sample <pid> 20` on a looping timedemo (`prof_loop.cfg` in `home.noindex/main/`: `set nextdemo "exec prof_loop.cfg"` then `demo bench_mohdm6`) gives clean call trees; leave out `CL_DemoCompleted` (the reloads) and the limiter's `NET_Sleep`. xctrace's Time Profiler (`--attach <pid>`) can't unwind through cgame.dylib (unloaded and reloaded per demo), so its shares are skewed, but its leaf addresses give per-instruction hot spots: subtract the load slide from the trace's `load-addr` and match an `objdump --disassemble-symbols=_<fn>` of the same binary. `sample` inflates the frame (0.41 → ~0.45 ms).
- Temporary counters printed from `RE_EndFrame` (`tr_cmds.c`) every N frames are a quick way to get per-frame workload numbers (vertices, lights per vertex); revert them before committing.

Gotchas found in session 9:
- **dm6 view 7 (the spawned soldier) can differ in one run:** once in session 9 a Metal run showed 574589 pixels off (a slightly moved view, game side); the next run matched GL1 again (1 pixel). GL1 runs agree bit for bit. If it happens, rerun the Metal side (`port/shot.sh fixed metal dm6 shot_dm6.cfg`, then `port/shot.sh views dm6`).
- **`port/build.sh` wipes a build tree that was configured from another source tree** (the old `gl` tree pointed at the repo root). Its default flavor is now `metal`.
- **`build.noindex/metalref-install`** was a scratch build of the pre-deletion GL1 + Metal (dylib) for the static-link A/B; deleted at the end of session 9. To rebuild it: configure `build.noindex/gl-src` with `-DBUILD_RENDERER_METAL=ON` (see §2 Phase 4).
- **`.github/workflows` still pass the removed options** (`USE_RENDERER_DLOPEN`, `BUILD_RENDERER_GL2`) and can't compile the Metal shaders without the toolchain: other-platform CI goes in Phase 7 (deleted in 7a, session 15: all workflows).
- The `seta cl_renderer` of an old config is written back as `seta cl_renderer "metal"` (the user's archive flag stays); harmless.

Gotchas found in session 8:
- **The Bash tool runs zsh:** `for p in "a b" …; do cmd $p; done` passes "a b" as one argument; use `${=p}`.
- **`com_target_game 1/2` writes into `home.noindex/mainta/` / `maintt/`** (screenshots, configs). `shot.sh` collects `main*/screenshots` now.
- **`r_showtris`/`r_shownormals` need `developer 1`.** Cvars the renderer registers late (like a scratch cvar) need `set` in a cfg; the bare `name value` form is silently ignored when the cvar doesn't exist yet.
- **Commands after `demo` in a cfg or on the command line didn't run** (so `video` couldn't be tested).
- **The system Metal shader cache (`$(getconf DARWIN_USER_CACHE_DIR)com.apple.metal`) is shared by all apps:** don't clear it to measure cold compiles. A new pipeline variant shows the cold cost by itself (42–56 ms here).
- **The pipeline cache lives in `home.noindex/metal/`** for our runs; delete it to measure a run without it, or set `r_metalPipelineCache 0`.
- **A missing `quit` at the end of a shot cfg costs shot.sh's 120 s alarm per run.**

Gotchas found in session 7:
- **Fixed views only compare deterministic things:**
  - `tele` keeps velocity: let a spawn fall die out in noclip first (`wait 2000`);
  - spawned actors walk off, so use `spawn script_model model <tiki>`. `spawn` places the entity 40 units ahead and 40 up: spawn from 40 below the floor to stand it on the floor;
  - firing, grenades, `cg_acidtrip` and (since the compiler flag) dm5's snow differ run to run. Check a new view with two runs of one renderer (`port/shot.sh fixed metal <name>B …`) before reading a GL1 difference as a renderer one.
- **mohdm6's "spawned soldier" view (dm6 view 7) mostly shows a close wall:** the soldier is barely in it. `shot_dm6fx.cfg` view 2 is the real model view.
- **`port/shot.sh` runs the `metal` install for Metal and the `gl` reference for GL1;** `OMM_FLAVOR=<flavor>` / `OMM_GL_FLAVOR=<flavor>` run other ones (e.g. a scratch build in build.noindex/).
- **`lldb --batch` stops at a crash without running the following `-o` commands:** use `-k "bt 40"` (`--source-on-crash`).
- **Grenade timing:** a frag grenade thrown from a cfg (`useweaponclass grenade`, `+attack`, `wait 500`, `-attack`) explodes ~4.5 s after the release.
- **No PIL here:** `port/tgamontage.py out.tga <columns> <downscale> a.tga b.tga …` tiles screenshots to look at them side by side; `sips -s format png` converts TGA → PNG.

Gotchas found in session 6:
- **In zsh, `log` is a builtin:** use `/usr/bin/log show …` for the unified log (gamepolicyd: `--predicate 'process == "gamepolicyd"'`, look for "gaming session" and "Game mode status").
- **Instruments' displayed-surfaces table has `detachment-reason` and `detachment-suggestion` columns** next to `direct-to-display`. `display_trace.py` prints the reason; `PROCESS=<name>` points it at another process.
- **Window latency changes with the compositor's mode, from run to run** (2.4–13 ms p50 this session). Measure windows several times, or trace them; compare display modes in one sitting.
- **The user's display-tint daemon (`~/.local/bin/dusk tint`) is running:** it overrides display gamma tables (GL1's hardware ramp), so don't judge GL1's gamma/overbright by eye on this Mac. Never stop it; it's the user's.
- **`GAMMA:` in the startup log always says 0 overbright bits** (printed before `R_SetColorMappings`); run `gfxinfo` later in the run for the real value.
- **Fullscreen runs reach Game Mode**, which may shift scheduling. Compare modes in one sitting. *Measured in session 64 (§2 "Session 64"): the same latency and mean frame work on and off, the bench's p95–p99 frame work higher with it on; gamepolicyd's log says when it is on (`/usr/bin/log show --predicate 'process == "gamepolicyd"'`: "Game mode status is now on"; zsh's own `log` builtin shadows the tool).*

Gotchas found in session 5:
- **`port/latency.sh` takes over the mouse:** the game window grabs it, and synthetic moves are posted for the run's length, about 30 s per run. Every run in session 5 got the keyboard focus by itself. If the user clicks elsewhere, SDL ignores the mouse and the run has no input frames. Check the screen lock first (the script does).
- **Instruments' display labels are misleading:**
  - the 240 Hz G2524H shows up as "external-0" with resolution (3840,2160), and the 60 Hz 4K as "external-1" (1920,1080): tell displays apart by their swap rate;
  - `Frame N` in surface labels starts at 1 with the first present inside the trace and wraps at 1000;
  - the presented-handler table's "Requested Time" is not on the host clock.

  `port/display_trace.py` handles all of this.
- Traces are ~0.3 GB each in `build.noindex/latency/`; `latency.sh` keeps them, so delete them after use.
- ~~Core Animation's present feedback in fullscreen with vsync off is wrong~~: fixed by going direct to display (session 6); still true for a composited fullscreen (GL1).
- macOS `sed` has no `\|` in basic regexes (use `grep -E`/awk). In zsh, `${=var}` word-splits a string variable.
- Session 4's gotchas still apply:
  - the Bash tool runs zsh (use arrays or `${=A}` for several args);
  - `wait N` with `fixedtime` continues after N/msec − 1 frames;
  - several `screenshot`s in one frame overwrite each other;
  - `r_drawworld 0` does nothing;
  - cheats need `+set thereisnomonkey 1`;
  - the weapon bar highlight runs on a real-time clock;
  - most maps crash when loaded locally (session 7: the clang bug, §3.2).
- Sessions 1–3's gotchas still apply:
  - check `CGSSessionScreenIsLocked` before measuring;
  - never pace frames on completed handlers;
  - test cfgs get a prefix (`shot_`, `lat_`);
  - `g_gametype 0 +devmap` needs `finishloadingscreen`;
  - the renderer's `vid_restart` is queued after pending cfg commands;
  - `screencapture` and ScreenCaptureKit have no permission (`CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess` 0), but posting events does;
  - stale PID files block on the "Abnormal Exit" dialog;
  - `s_initsound 0` crashes;
  - use `sv_maxclients` ≥ 2 for scripted map loads;
  - `glconfig_t` is ABI;
  - HiDPI input on 2× displays is untested (§6 of session 4: `SDL_WINDOWEVENT_RESIZED` compares points with pixels, relative mouse deltas are in points, `SDL_WarpMouseInWindow` expects points).

Open bugs:
- **In the renderer:** none known. (The depth/stencil readback stubs are gone, session 8.)
- **Frame pacing against the display:** session 29's queued presents at exact 250 fps on the 240 Hz display during an unidentified ~10-minute condition (§6 above, Phase 5 "Session 29 result").
- **Display path:** the window's latency depends on the compositor's mode (§2). In exclusive fullscreen and the borderless window, another application drawing on the other display delays our flips (the WindowServer's, p95 +~2 ms); late presents keep every frame shown (session 26), the Space avoids it on this Mac by blanking that display. (GL1's fullscreen never went direct; GL1 is gone, the reference flavor keeps it for comparisons only.)
- **The cursor in the fullscreen Space** (session 73, seen once online, parked): the system cursor stuck at the center while captured, cleared by Cmd+Tab (§6 "Where things stand (end of session 73)").
- **Outside it:** none known. (Session 19's failed pipeline-cache save: found and fixed in session 27, Phase 5 "Session 27 result".) The local map-load crash was the Apple clang 21 `MergeCompatibleInvokes` bug; the build flag fixes it (§3.2 session 7). Drop the flag once Xcode fixes the bug.
- **Untested:**
  - ~~HiDPI input~~: the mouse replay on the 2× display (session 21: the UI's cursor in pixels; the resize check compares pixels since 6b); a real mouse on the 2× display with the native flavor is still unchecked;
  - video capture (`video`; synchronous by design, see §3.2 session 8);
  - swipes and mirrors (no retail content reaches them, §3.2 session 7); real map flare surfaces (none in retail; tested with a scratch hook);
  - ~~exclusive fullscreen at a non-native resolution (a display mode change), and fullscreen on the 4K@2× display~~: tested in session 19 (direct on every frame: 1280×720 @ 240 Hz on SDL and native, native exclusive on the 4K at 3840×2160); the Space and the borderless window on the 4K are still untested;
  - ~~exclusive fullscreen's focus loss on the native layer (needs a real Cmd+Tab, 6f)~~: the user's Cmd+Tab in session 25 (at the desktop's mode through the system's switcher; with a mode switch through `MacOS_SwitchKey`); a mode switch on a display other than the main one (`CGDisplayCapture` of that display only) is still untested;
  - GCMouse's clicks against the button events in a polled loop (session 21's measurement used an idle run loop).
